Nothing bounded `at + count` before the unchecked additions in `insert_lines` (the "Format Same As Above" loop `at..at + count`) and `delete_lines` (the block end `at + count - 1` and the shift origin `at + count`). With overflow checks on, those panicked and `Session::execute` returned `EngineError::Internal`. In release builds they wrapped.

**Insert:** `insert_lines` now checks `at.checked_add(count)` against `MAX_ROWS` / `MAX_COLS` before doing anything else and returns `BadParams` for the command when the new lines would run past the end of the worksheet. This is the same check `sheet.moveColumns` already uses (`checked_add` + `is_none_or(|end| end > MAX_COLS)` → `bad("sheet.moveColumns", …)`). The existing "cannot shift nonblank cells off of the worksheet" guard is unchanged, and it still catches data being pushed off the sheet.

**Delete:** `delete_lines` clamps `count` to the lines left from `at` to the end of the worksheet. The block end was already clamped with `.min(MAX_ROWS - 1)`, so the existing intent was already "delete up to the end of the sheet". Clamping `count` first means the shift origin and `Edit::Delete` get the same, representable count.

`home.insertCells` / `home.deleteCells` with `shift: row|column` go through the same two functions, so they are covered too.

Tests (`crates/engine/tests/line_count_overflow.rs`), all on both axes:
- insert with `count: u32::MAX` returns `BadParams`
- insert after a line with a custom height/width and no cells (the formatting-only state from the issue, where the used-range guard has nothing to check) returns `BadParams`. Without the fix this hits the overflowing loop.
- delete with `count: u32::MAX` doesn't return `Internal`
- a normal insert/delete of 3 rows still works

title: Formula: print flat operator chains iteratively so deep trees cannot overflow the stack (#527)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #527.

A flat chain like `1+1+1+...` passes the parser's nesting guard but builds a left-nested tree with one `Binary` level per operator. `write_expr` recursed into the left child for every level, so canonical printing (`print` and `print_r1c1`, and `Formula::new` / `Formula::from_expr`, which call `print`) used stack proportional to the chain length.

The `Expr::Binary` arm now walks the left spine in a loop, collects `(op, right)` pairs, prints the leftmost operand, then appends each operator and right operand in order. The output text is unchanged; right operands and every other node kind are printed as before. A1 and R1C1 share this arm, so both are covered.

Not changed: the parser's nesting guard, and the guarded English/Spanish display in `print_input`, which keeps rejecting such trees with "formula is nested too deeply".

Test: `prints_long_flat_chain_without_deep_recursion` builds a 20000-term `+` chain and prints it with `print` and `print_r1c1` on a thread with a 256 KB stack, then checks the exact text. Without the fix the recursive printer overflows that stack.

title: Make check --json list warning messages instead of a count (#526)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #526.

`docs/cli.md` documents the `warnings` field of each file in `gridcraft-check/1` as the list of import-warning messages (`"warnings": ["..."]`), but `check --json` emitted only the number of warnings and left out the texts.

`FileReport.warnings` now keeps the `Vec<String>` that `gridcraft_engine::io::open_bytes` returns, in order, so the JSON report emits an array of strings (an empty array when there are no warnings). This matches the documented schema, so no docs change is needed. Nothing else read the count.

Test: `json_lists_warning_messages` checks that a file with one warning gets `["..."]` and a file without warnings gets `[]`.

title: Cap queued pointer events from ui.click/ui.drag control requests (#525)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #525.

`ui.click` and `ui.drag` built their whole synthetic event queue from the request's `count` / `steps` with no upper bound, so one control request could allocate an arbitrarily large queue and still reply `ok: true` (AGENTS.md asks for caps on allocations sized by control parameters).

**Change** (`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs`)
- New `MAX_QUEUED_POINTER_EVENTS = 10_000` budget. `push_click` and `push_drag` first check that the already-queued events plus the events the request would add fit in it; if not, they return an error and leave the queue unchanged (nothing is pushed or allocated).
- All four entry points that use these helpers (`ui.click`, `ui.drag`, `ui.cell.click`, `ui.cell.drag`) return that error the same way the other control commands report failures (`err(...)`).
- `count` / `steps` are clamped to `u32::MAX` before the cast, so a huge JSON value can no longer wrap to a small one.
- Accepted requests behave as before: same event order, positions, default count (1) and default drag steps (8); the cell geometry guards and the fixed 8-step cell drag are unchanged.

**Docs**: `docs/control-protocol.md` notes the limit on the pointer rows.

**Test**: `oversized_pointer_requests_are_refused_and_leave_the_queue_alone` checks that a double click still queues 5 events, that oversized clicks and drags (including one that only overflows because of events already queued) are refused with the queue left exactly as it was, and that a normal 3-step drag still queues in full afterwards.

title: Page Setup opens on the sheet's saved margins (#524)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #524.

The Page Setup form always opened on the Normal preset (0.7, 0.7, 0.75, 0.75, 0.3, 0.3), so OK with no edits overwrote custom or Wide margins with Normal. With one field edited, OK applied that field and reset the other five to Normal.

The `pageSetup` form now reads its six defaults from the active sheet's `print.margins`. Row Height, Column Width and Zoom already open on the current sheet value in the same way. A sheet with no saved margins still falls back to the Normal numbers. The values are rounded to 4 decimals so that a stored f32 such as 0.1 shows as 0.1 and not 0.10000000149. Writing the rounded value back gives the same f32.

Every way into the dialog uses the same builder: Page Layout > Margins > Custom Margins, File > Print > Page Setup, the PSP KeyTip, `ui.dialog` with `"name": "pageSetup"`, and the Print Titles button, which passes `{"tab": "Sheet"}`. OK and `ui.dialog.confirm` both submit the form values, so the fix covers them too. Cancel already wrote nothing.

Paper, orientation, scale and print-title controls are still not in the form. The issue says that is separate work.

Tests (`crates/ui-egui/tests/page_setup_margins.rs`). Both fail on `main`:
- `page_setup_ok_without_edits_keeps_custom_margins`: sets the issue's margins (2, 2.5, 3, 0.25, 0.1, 0.2). Opens the dialog bare and with the Print Titles `{"tab": "Sheet"}` argument. Checks that the form shows those six numbers and that an unedited OK leaves them unchanged.
- `page_setup_one_edited_field_keeps_the_other_margins`: changes only left to 1.5. The other five stay at the custom values.

title: Open the Header & Footer dialog on the sheet's saved header and footer (#523)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #523.

The Header & Footer dialog (keytip F10 N H 1, or `ui.dialog` with `headerFooter`) always opened with an empty header and the footer `&CPage &P of &N`. Pressing OK without edits then sent those two strings through `pageLayout.headerFooter` and replaced the sheet's saved header and footer.

The form now starts from the active sheet's `print.header` and `print.footer`, the same way the Row Height, Column Width and comment forms start from the current document value. With no active sheet it falls back to empty strings. Both entry paths go through `Dialog::new`, so both are fixed. The dialog still carries only the ordinary header and footer, so the first-page and even-page strings and their flags are not touched. The in-place Page Layout editor is unchanged.

Test: `header_footer_dialog_opens_on_the_saved_header_and_footer` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/interaction.rs` sets `&LLeft` / `&CConfidential`, opens the dialog, checks that the fields show those strings, then changes only the header to `&CNew` and checks that the footer stays `&CConfidential`. It fails on main, where the fields open as `""` and `&CPage &P of &N`.

title: Data Validation dialog opens on the active cell's current rule (#522)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #522.

The Data Validation form always opened on fixed defaults (an empty list rule). Its OK runs `data.validation`, which replaces the rule on the selection, so confirming the dialog without edits replaced a working rule with an empty list that rejects every non-blank value.

The form now starts from the rule stored on the active cell, the same way Row Height, Column Width, Zoom and Format Cells start from the current value they edit. Type, operator, formulas, Ignore blank, In-cell dropdown, error style and the input/error titles and messages are all read from the rule, so OK without edits stores the same rule again. A cell without a rule still opens on the old blank list defaults.

Every entry path (Data menu, native menu, `ui.dialog` with `dataValidation`, and `data.validation` with no type) goes through `Dialog::open`, so all of them are covered. The `data.validation` command itself is unchanged: a call that names a type still replaces the target range.

Tests in `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`:
- `data_validation_opens_on_the_rule_of_the_active_cell`: puts a whole number > 5 rule on A1, opens the dialog, checks the form shows `whole` / `greater` / `5`, presses OK without edits, and checks that `6` is still accepted and `4` rejected. Fails on main.
- `data_validation_without_a_rule_opens_on_a_blank_list`: a cell without a rule still opens on the list defaults.

title: Zoom dialog: a Magnification choice sets the percentage to store (#521)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #521.

The Zoom dialog always opens with `percent` set to the current sheet zoom. Clicking a Magnification entry only wrote `preset`. The OK builder copies `preset` into `percent` only when `percent` is missing, so OK and `ui.dialog.confirm` both ran `view.zoom` with the old percentage.

The fix adds `Dialog::set_value`. In the Zoom dialog, setting `preset` also sets `percent` to that magnification. Both ways of changing a form value use it: the Magnification radio buttons and `ui.dialog.set` on the control channel. That covers every path the issue lists: the OK button, `ui.dialog.confirm`, and a choice set over the control channel. A later Custom (%) edit still writes `percent`, so it wins. An unedited OK still stores the current zoom.

Tests (`crates/ui-egui/tests/zoom_dialog.rs`), following the issue's restoration check:
- 160 → click `50%` → real OK button → 50
- 180 → click `75%` → `ui.dialog.confirm` → 75
- 180 → `ui.dialog.set preset 25` → `ui.dialog.confirm` → 25
- `preset 25`, then Custom (%) 225 → 225; reopen and OK with no edits → stays 225

The first three fail on main, where the zoom stays at 160, 180 and 180.

title: Fix ribbon checkboxes sending the pre-click value (#520)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #520.

Five ribbon checkboxes (View > Formula Bar, Page Layout > Sheet Options View/Print Gridlines and View/Print Headings) ran their command with `on: !v`. egui has already flipped `v` when `resp.changed()` is true, so a click stored the value from before the click and the setting never changed.

The handlers now use a small helper, `checkbox_on(clicked, shown)`:
- On a click, the checkbox bool already holds the new choice, so it is sent as is. This matches the View tab Gridlines, Headings and Ruler checkboxes, which already send the post-click value.
- On a key tip routed to the control (`invoke`, used by WVF for the formula bar), the bool is unchanged, so the command gets the opposite and the key tip still toggles. The Page Layout key tips (PVG, PVH, PPG, PPH) and WVG/WVH run the commands directly and are not affected.

Only `crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs` changes. Test `click_sends_the_new_checkbox_value_and_key_tip_the_opposite` checks both paths of the helper: a click sends the new checkbox value, a key tip sends the toggled value.

title: Keep a literal chart category with a comma or semicolon as one point on save (#519)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #519.

Reading a `<c:strLit>` category stores each point as one quoted element of an array constant (`a,b` becomes `{"a,b"}`, with `"` doubled), but `str_data` split that text on every `,` and `;` when saving. So a label like `a,b` or `a;b` was written as two points next to a single value.

`str_data` now splits array constants with a small helper, `split_array_items`, that only treats `,` and `;` as separators outside double quotes and reads `""` inside quotes as a literal quote, which is the inverse of how `data_ref` builds the constant on read. Unquoted items are still trimmed as before, and spaces around a quoted item are still dropped, so `{ "Jan" , "Feb" }` keeps saving as `Jan`, `Feb`.

Not changed: series names (they never went through the splitter), cell-reference categories, and numeric literals (`num_data`, numbers cannot contain these separators).

Test: `tests::literal_category_roundtrip` saves and re-reads a chart whose categories are `{"a,b"}`, `{"a;b"}`, `{"red","blue"}`, a label with embedded quotes and a comma, a mixed three-item list, and a spaced array constant, and checks every category and the `North, South` series name come back unchanged. Without the fix it fails on `{"a,b"}`, which comes back as `{"a","b"}`.

title: Read omitted val on chart smooth and showVal as on (#518)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #518.

`c:smooth` and `c:showVal` are `CT_Boolean`, so an element with no `val` attribute means on (ECMA-376). The chart reader already handles this through `bool_val` for a trendline's `dispEq` and `dispRSqr`. Series smoothing and the value-label check used their own parsing instead:

- `smooth` parsed `val` as a number, so `<c:smooth/>` and `<c:smooth val="true"/>` read as off.
- The `show_val` closure accepted only `"1"` or `"true"`, so `<c:showVal/>` read as off.

Both now call `bool_val`, like the trendline flags. The writer already writes these flags from the model, so once the read is correct, open-then-save keeps them on.

The change is in `crates/xlsx/src/chart.rs` only. `read_series` is shared by every chart type, scatter included. The `show_val` closure covers both the group's `dLbls` and each series' `dLbls`.

Tests: the new `crates/xlsx/src/tests/chart_bool_default.rs` reads the chart XML from the issue. With no `val`, both flags read on, and so does a series-level `<c:showVal/>`. `val="1"` and `val="true"` read on. `val="0"` reads off, and so does a chart without the elements. Without the fix, the omitted-`val` case and `<c:smooth val="true"/>` fail.

title: Fix saving a custom view or script when the stored list is not a JSON object (#517)
author: MarekSpodBiedry

title: Treat non-object params as empty in themeColors, background and drawBorder (#516)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #516.

`pageLayout.themeColors`, `pageLayout.background` and `home.drawBorder` clone their params and then assign keys (`params["name"]`, `params["alt"]`/`params["at"]`, `params["preset"]`). serde_json panics on a key assignment into an array, number, string or boolean, so these calls ended up as `EngineError::Internal` through the last-resort guard in `Session::execute`. The control channel, the CLI and saved script steps can pass such values.

A small `object_params` helper in `cmd/extra.rs` now copies the params as an object and treats any non-object value as no params, the same way `null` is already handled. It uses the same `p.as_object().cloned().unwrap_or_default()` idiom as the `with` helpers in `format.rs`, `insert.rs` and `pivot.rs`. The three wrappers use it, so `[]`, `5`, `"x"` and `true` now behave like `{}` (`Ok(null)` on an open workbook). Behaviour for object and `null` params does not change. These three functions were the only places in the engine that assigned keys into caller-supplied params.

Test: `tests::non_object_params_do_not_panic_in_wrapper_commands` runs each of the three commands with `[]`, `5`, `"x"` and `true`, and runs a saved script whose `home.drawBorder` step has `[]` params. It asserts that no call returns an internal error. Without the fix, every case fails.

title: Refuse a PivotTable that cannot fit before aggregating all column groups (#515)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #515.

`pivot::compute` built every `(row prefix, column prefix)` accumulator vector (one `Acc` per value field) for the whole source before it counted the report's data columns and returned "The PivotTable report will not fit on the sheet." With many value fields, a report that was going to be refused anyway allocated all of that storage first; the existing `aggs.len() > 5_000_000` guard counts keys, not the value fields stored at each key.

**Change**

- While aggregating, `compute` now tracks the distinct column leaves seen so far (the column path cut after the first collapsed item, exactly as `flatten_cols` lays them out). After each record it checks whether `(leaves + grand-total column) × value fields` already exceeds `MAX_COLS`, and if so returns the same "will not fit on the sheet" error the later data-column check returns. That product is a lower bound on the final data-column count (subtotal columns only add to it), so a report that fits is never refused; the refusal just happens as soon as it is certain, before accumulators for further column groups are allocated.
- Collapsed column items are counted as one column group, so collapsing does not cause a false refusal of a report that fits.
- The later exact `data_cols` check is unchanged and still catches every other case.

**Tests**

- `pivot::fit_tests::column_budget_counts_value_fields_and_grand_total`: the bound helper.
- `cmd::pivot::tests::too_many_value_columns_are_refused`: the issue's fixture (64 × 64 records, `Cat` on Rows, `Sub` on Columns): 256 repeated `V` value fields are refused with the fit error, 128 still succeed. (The error text is the same as before; this pins that the early check refuses exactly what the final check would and nothing more. The point of refusal itself is covered by the helper test above.)
- `cmd::pivot::tests::collapsed_column_items_count_as_one_column_group`: 256 value fields with `Grp` collapsed and 64 `Sub` items added under it still fit (one column group plus t…

title: Fail Web Page export on sheets taller than its row limit instead of dropping cells (#514)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #514.

Save as Web Page walked at most 100,001 rows from the first used row and reported success, so with `near` in A1 and `far` in A150000 the HTML had no `far`. The issue allows either a complete table or a clear error.

This keeps the existing row budget, but `to_html` now returns `Result`. If the used range is taller than 100,001 rows it fails with "the sheet is too tall for a web page (N rows, at most 100001). Save as .xlsx or CSV instead." instead of returning a partial table. When the sheet fits, it writes every row of the used range as before. The error has the same form as the other `save_bytes` refusals (`.xls`/`.xlsb`/`.ods`: "Save as .xlsx or another supported export format."). `file.saveBytes`, `file.exportHtml` and Save/Save As to `.html`/`.htm` all go through `save_bytes`, so each of them now returns this error. `to_html` has no other callers. The clipboard HTML fragment is a separate path with its own 10,000-cell limit and is not changed.

`docs/file-format-parity.md` now states the limit in the `.htm`/`.html` row.

Test: `html_export_fails_instead_of_dropping_cells_past_the_row_limit` runs the issue's two cases through `save_bytes`: A1 + A150000 must give an error (on main it succeeds without `far`), and A1 + A100001 must succeed with both values.

title: xlsx: warn when hyperlinks past the 10,000-cell cap are dropped on read (#513)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #513.

`read_hyperlinks` in `crates/xlsx/src/sheet_read.rs` stops after 10,000 hyperlink cells per `hyperlinks` element (`MAX_HYPERLINK_CELLS`). It stopped without a warning, so a sheet with 12,000 links opened with only 10,000 links and an empty `ReadReport::warnings`. The next save then wrote only the shorter list.

This PR keeps the cap, because it protects against hostile whole-grid ranges and `huge_coordinates_and_dimensions` relies on it. When the cap stops the read, the reader now adds a warning: `sheet "<name>": hyperlinks past the first 10000 cells were dropped`. The wording follows the existing `sheet "<name>": ... were dropped` warning for cells outside the grid in the same function. The warning goes through the read report, so File > Open shows it in the existing notice.

A sheet with exactly 10,000 hyperlink cells or fewer gets no warning. The warning is added only when there is a further cell that would be dropped.

Test: `hyperlinks_past_the_cell_cap_are_reported` in `crates/xlsx/src/tests/malformed.rs` reads `<hyperlink ref="A1:A12000" location="x"/>` with a styles part present. It checks that 10,000 links are kept and that the warning is in the report. It also reads a three-link control sheet and checks that all 3 links come back with no warnings. Without the fix, the warning check fails.

title: Keep every range of a conditional format or validation sqref (#512)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #512.

`parse_sqref` cut every `sqref` list at 10,000 ranges with `.take(10_000)` and reported nothing. A conditional format or data validation with more ranges lost the rest on open, and the next save wrote the shorter list.

The cap is removed. `parse_sqref` is the one reader for conditional formats, main data validations and Excel 2010 (x14) validations (the x14 `xm:sqref` child goes through the same function), so all three paths are fixed. The list is already bounded by the size of the XML, and the other `sqref` reader in this file (line 256) already keeps every range with no cap.

Test: `sqref_keeps_more_than_ten_thousand_ranges` parses 12,000 single-cell ranges and checks that all 12,000 come back, ending at `A12000`. It fails on main (10,000).

title: Save a table that has only a header row and a totals row (#511)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #511.

Insert Table on a single row followed by Total Row leaves a table that is a header row plus a totals row with no data row (e.g. `A1:B2`). `write_sheet` in `crates/xlsx/src/sheet_write.rs` only kept a table when it was taller than header + totals, or when it was header-only, so this shape matched neither arm and was dropped silently: no table part, no `tableParts`, no warning. The name, style, banding, first/last column flags, filter and totals metadata were lost on reopen.

The filter now also keeps a table with a header row whenever there is room for that header above the totals row. That makes header + totals behave like the header-only and one-data-row shapes, which already save. Tables without a header row keep the old rule, so nothing else changes. The reader (`read_table`) already loads this shape, so it now round-trips.

Test: `header_and_totals_table_without_data_row_survives` in `crates/xlsx/src/tests/roundtrip.rs` writes an `A1:B2` header + totals table and reads it back. It checks for one table with no warnings, the same range, name, style, banding and first/last column flags, the totals label and totals function, and the header cell rewritten to the column name. Without the fix the read-back has zero tables.

title: Keep a long outline group's bracket once its first 4096 lines scroll away (#510)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #510.

`outline::layout` found the first on-screen detail line of an expanded group with `(grp.start..=grp.end).take(4096)`. When a group was longer than 4096 lines and the view was past its first 4096 lines, nothing was found, so the bracket was not drawn. This happened for rows and for columns.

The search is now in `Dir::first_visible`. It checks the frozen lines in the group first. Then it checks the scrolling lines, starting at the line at the scrolling pane's edge (`Geo::row_at` / `Geo::col_at` at the split). It does not start at the group's first line. The search stays short for any group length, and there is no cap. The rest of the bracket code did not change: the tick shows only when the group's first line is on screen, the − / + button stays on the summary line, and the level buttons are the same.

Test: `outline::tests::long_groups_keep_their_bracket_past_4096_lines` makes a 5000-line expanded group on each axis, with a viewport of 800 × 600. At scroll lines 0, 4095, 4096, 4200 and 4970 it checks that there is one bracket, and that the bracket has a tick only at line 0. When the view is past the group's summary line, it checks that there is no bracket. On main, the test fails at line 4096.

title: fix(grid): filter dropdown installs the AutoFilter on the clicked table (#509)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #509.

With two tables stacked in the same column and no sheet AutoFilter yet, clicking the lower table's header filter button installed the AutoFilter on the upper table. `filter_menu` looked the table up with `.find(|t| t.range.start.row <= at.y as u32 || true)`, a predicate that is always true, so it kept the first table in sheet order and only then checked the column. The dropdown's value list comes from the installed AutoFilter, so it listed and filtered the wrong table.

The fix:
- `GridState::filter_menu` now also stores the row of the clicked header cell (the click handler already has it as `c.row`); this is the only place that opens the menu.
- A small `filter_table_range(sheet, col, row)` helper picks the table whose header row is that row and whose columns contain the clicked column. This is the same row/column test `Sheet::has_filter_button` uses to decide that a table header cell gets a button at all. Tables cannot overlap, so at most one table matches.

A sheet with only one table still installs that table's range, and a sheet that already has an AutoFilter is unchanged (the on-demand install is skipped, as before).

Test in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`: `filter_menu_uses_the_table_whose_header_was_clicked` puts tables over A1:A3 and A5:A8 (the issue's layout). Clicking A5 picks A5:A8, clicking A1 picks A1:A3, and a click outside both tables' columns picks none. With the old lookup the A5 click picked A1:A3.

title: Keep manually hidden and collapsed rows when removing an AutoFilter (#508)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #508.

Removing the sheet AutoFilter (`data.filter` toggled off) cleared the hidden flag of every row on the sheet. Rows hidden by hand, rows in a collapsed outline group and rows outside the filter range all became visible, even when the filter had no criteria. The collapsed group's summary row stayed marked collapsed while its detail rows showed.

Now the removal branch of `toggle_filter` unhides only the rows that `Sheet::is_row_filtered` reports as hidden by the filter. It collects those rows before it clears `autofilter`. Other hidden rows keep their state. A filter with criteria still reveals the rows it hid, so the issue's criterion-only control keeps working.

Both triggers in the issue are covered:
- **Direct removal**: `data.filter` run twice on A1:A4.
- **Table dropdown with the active cell outside the table**: `filter_menu` in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs` installs its on-demand AutoFilter by running `data.filter` twice. The second call reaches the same removal branch, so this fix covers that path too, and the UI code needs no change.

Tests (both fail on `main`):
- `removing_an_autofilter_keeps_manually_hidden_and_collapsed_rows`: rows 2-4 grouped and collapsed, row 10 hidden by hand. After the filter is installed and removed, the same rows stay hidden, row 5 stays collapsed, and no AutoFilter is left.
- `table_dropdown_setup_outside_the_table_keeps_manually_hidden_rows`: a table on A1:A4, rows 3 and 10 hidden by hand, E1 selected, then the dropdown's two `data.filter` calls. Rows 3 and 10 stay hidden.

title: Run the fill-handle double-click fill before the handle press returns (#507)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #507.

A double-click is also reported as a click, so a press on the fill handle armed `Drag::Fill` and returned before the double-click fill block further down in `interact` was reached. With an idle frame between the two clicks (a normal double-click), the fill never ran.

The fill-handle double-click block now runs before the press handling, next to the header AutoFit double-click, and follows the same pattern: it clears the drag state, requests focus and returns. The neighbour-column scan itself is unchanged (it is moved, not rewritten), so it does not overlap with #210 / #451.

Unchanged: dragging the handle still fills the series, and a double-click on an ordinary cell still starts the editor (that path does not touch the handle).

Test: `crates/ui-egui/tests/fill_handle_double_click.rs` drives real egui pointer events with one idle frame between the clicks on the B3 handle, then checks that B4:B6 = 40, 50, 60, the selection is B1:B6, and `edit.autoFill` ran once. This is the issue's repro sequence, which leaves B4:B6 empty on main.

title: Center Across Selection: center text over the empty cells to its right (#479)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #479.

Center Across Selection (`centerContinuous` in XLSX) was drawn like plain Center: the text was centred in its own cell only. In Excel the text is centred over the cell plus the run of empty cells to its right that also use Center Across Selection, without merging.

**Grid (`crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`)**
- New helper `center_across_end` finds the last column of the run: following cells that are empty (not merged) and also Center Across. The run stops at the first cell with content, another alignment, or a merge.
- The cell's clip rect is widened to the run (the gridlines inside it are painted over, as for text overflow), and the text is centred on that rect. This covers numbers too, as in Excel.
- Wrapped, rotated and merged cells keep their current behaviour.

**Print / PDF export (`crates/engine/src/cmd/print.rs`)**
- The same bug was in the print path, which mapped Center Across to Center. New helper `center_across_width` gives the width of the same run, and `draw_text` centres and clips the text over it. The page edge still clips it.

**Tests**
- `grid::tests::center_across_run_stops_at_first_non_continuing_column`: the run-length helper.
- `print::tests::center_across_spans_following_empty_center_across_cells`: the run covers the empty Center Across cells, stops at a cell with content, and stops at a merged cell.

Text wider than the run is clipped to the run. It does not spill further into neighbouring cells.

title: i18n: add Polish (pl) interface
author: brzuchal
body:
## Summary

Adds Polish (`pl`) as an interface language, in the same shape as the Czech (https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/pull/335) and French (https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/pull/413) tables.

- `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/pl.rs`: all **381** keys of the reference (Japanese) table.
- `i18n.rs`: `Language::Pl` (name "Polski", code `pl`, system tags `pl-*` / `pl_*`), appended to the end of `ALL`, so the switcher lists it last.

- `docs/localization-parity.md` and `ROADMAP.md` list Polish under the other shipped languages.

Like the other tables, this covers only what the ribbon catalog covers today (ribbon, sheet tabs, widgets, Backstage labels). Dialogs, menus, panes and messages stay English until the catalog grows.

No Microsoft Excel (or other product) localisation, string table or translated UI was consulted or copied. I am a native Polish speaker. The table was drafted with Claude (AI agent) and I went through every entry myself; no second native speaker has reviewed it yet.

## Format Cells dialog

The Format Cells dialog uses 56 labels. 20 of them were already in the Polish table (Number, Currency, Accounting, Left, Center, …), and `7aad174` adds the other 36 (Format Cells, Alignment, Font, Border, Protection, Wrap text, Shrink to fit, Bold, Italic, Subscript, Superscript, Locked, Hidden, No Color, Outline, Diagonal ↗/↘, Single/Double Accounting, …).

https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/pull/788 is merged, so the Format Cells dialog now looks these labels up and shows them in Polish. The other dialogs follow once https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/pull…

title: Outline follow-ups to #388: Rows / Columns dialog, Ungroup recalculates SUBTOTAL, − / + while editing (#373)
author: iluebbe
body:
Follow-up to #388 for #373 (I reported #373). I clicked through #388 in the running app (main at 3926d21) and found these left over.

## Problem

1. **Wrong totals after Ungroup.** In the sales sample, collapse rows 5:8 with the − button, select rows 4:9 and click Data ▸ Ungroup. The rows come back, but the Total row (`=SUBTOTAL(109,Sales[Q1])`) keeps showing $101,150 instead of $304,820 until F9. Saving in between writes the stale values.
2. **No Rows / Columns choice for a range of cells** (item 1 of #373, listed as not done in #388). Data ▸ Group, Alt+Shift+Right and Alt, A, G, G on B2:C5 always group rows. Excel asks.
3. **− / + while a cell is being edited.** Type into B6, then click − on row 9. Row 6 is hidden, but its editor stays open, drawn over row 9, and Enter writes into the hidden cell.
4. Show Detail, Hide Detail and Ungroup with nothing grouped at the selection still add an undo step. Ungrouping with a selection that ends on the summary row (4:9 above) leaves `collapsed="1"` on row 9 in the saved file.

## Cause

1. `group()` in `cmd/data.rs` unhides the lines it ungroups but doesn't ask for a full recalculation (`cx.structural`). Hide / Show Detail and Hide Rows do, because SUBTOTAL(10x) depends on hidden rows.
2. Every UI entry point ran `data.group` / `data.ungroup` directly; nothing asked for the `by` parameter #388 added.
3. The band's click handler in `grid.rs` runs its command without committing the editor. Other clicks on the sheet commit first.
4. `detail()` and `group()` always went through `edit()`, and the stale-summary check only looked at the line after the selection.

## Fix

- Engine: Ungroup sets `cx.structural` when it shows lines again, and clears `collapsed` on every line in or right after the range that is no longer a group's summary. Ungroup, Show Detail and Hide Detail return early, without an undo step, when there is nothing to act on.
- UI: `SheetApp::group_selection(on)` (un)groups whole rows or whole columns right away. Any …

title: i18n(cs): translate 120 labels and tooltips already looked up via tr()
author: Losminek
body:
Follow-up to #335 (Czech). 120 interface strings already go through `tr()` but had no Czech entry, so
a Czech user saw them in English. This PR adds those entries to `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/cs.rs` only.

## What changes

- Ribbon tooltips and menu items (101), cell/header context menus (11), formula bar (3), sheet tabs and
  status controls (5), notice dismissal (1).
- No new `tr()` call sites, no other language touched, no code changes. Extra Czech-only keys are fine
  for `translations_are_unique_and_preserve_unknown_text` (it requires the Japanese master keys in
  every language, not the reverse).

## How it was made and checked

AI-assisted translation with an independent review pass (every key matched against its call site;
terms follow the existing Czech catalog and Excel conventions: Průřez for slicers, Rukopis, Deník
akcí…). Not yet proofread by a native speaker; corrections are welcome.

Clean environment, `--locked`: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui
--all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui`: 590 passed, 1 failed — the
failure is `translations_are_unique_and_preserve_unknown_text` reporting the French row for
"Different First Page", which is missing on current `main` as well; Czech passes.

title: App icon: simplify the placeholder for small sizes, add a 16-32 px cut
author: reinhole
body:

title: cli, control: fix mcp source conflict, document run flags, cap request size
author: mosesamwoma
body:
Three small fixes found while reading the code:

- cli: `mcp --in FILE --sample NAME` silently ignored `--sample`, and `mcp --connect PORT --in FILE` silently ignored `--in`, while `run` rejects the first case. Both commands now share `session_from`, and `--connect` refuses a local source. Adds the regression test `mcp_rejects_conflicting_sources`.
- cli: `run`'s `--print RANGE|used`, `--sheet`, `--csv` and `--formulas` are documented in docs/cli.md and accepted by the code, but were missing from `--help` and the header comment in main.rs.

Not compiled or run locally (my environment has Rust 1.85, the repo needs 1.90), so please rely on CI.

title: Data: “Remove trailing zeros after the decimal separator” conversion option (#656)
author: vedran-dobos
body:
Fixes #656. **Builds on #583** (its option set, command and Options section); please review that

GridCraft's addition to the Automatic Data Conversion list, placed under its counterpart "Remove
leading zeros and convert to a number": **Remove trailing zeros after the decimal separator**, **on by
default**, so nothing changes until someone unchecks it.

## What changed
- **core** `DataConversion::remove_trailing_zeros` (default `true`, part of `all()`). Off, when

- **ui-egui** File › Options › Data: the checkbox under "Remove leading zeros"; its tooltip says it
  isn't an Excel option.

The value is always the plain number (`720.0` is 720 for formulas); only the format is added. Because

title: Functions: GROUPBY / PIVOTBY aggregate with a LAMBDA, PERCENTOF or CONCAT (builds on #486)
author: iluebbe
body:
Builds on #486 (functions passed by name): this branch contains its commit c7701f6. Please merge #486 first; after that this PR shows only its own commit (d8f45f5).

## Problem

`GROUPBY` / `PIVOTBY` only take one of their built-in aggregations (`SUM`, `AVERAGE`… or a code). Anything else is an error, while Excel accepts it:

| Formula | Excel | GridCraft (main) |
|---|---|---|
| `=GROUPBY(A1:A3,B1:B3,LAMBDA(x,SUM(x)))` | a 4 / b 2 / Total 6 | `#CALC!` |
| `=GROUPBY(A1:A3,B1:B3,PERCENTOF)` | a 0.667 / b 0.333 / Total 1 | `#VALUE!` (after #486) |
| `=GROUPBY(A1:A3,B1:B3,CONCAT)` | a "13" / b "2" / Total "123" | `#VALUE!` (after #486) |
| `=PIVOTBY(…,LAMBDA(x,y,SUM(x)/SUM(y)))` | share of the column group | `#CALC!` |

PIVOTBY also returns blanks for its corner cell and for row/column combinations without data. Excel returns empty text there (its cached value is `t="str"` with an empty `<v>`), so `gridcraft-cli check` reports `text → blank` on files saved by Excel.

## Cause

`crates/functions/src/dynamic.rs` resolves the aggregation with `parse_agg`, which knows only the built-in names. "Custom LAMBDA aggregations are not supported here" (module doc). A LAMBDA can't be called from the functions crate; the evaluator in `crates/calc` has to apply it, as it does for MAP / BYROW / SCAN.

## Fix

- `functions`: `groupby_with` / `pivotby_with` take the aggregation as a callback `(group values, values measured against) → value`. `groupby` / `pivotby` are those with the built-in aggregation, so built-in names behave exactly as before. `is_named_aggregation` says which names they handle themselves.
- `calc` (`GROUPBY` / `PIVOTBY` arm from #486): a LAMBDA (in place, from LET or from a defined name), or a function by name that isn't built in, goes through `group_with_lambda`. Behaviour observed in Excel (Microsoft 365) and copied:
  - The lambda gets one group's values, one value column at a time.
  - A second parameter gets the values the group is measured against. For GROUPBY…

title: XLSX: What-If scenarios as Excel's <scenarios>, kept on their sheet
author: iluebbe
body:
## Problem

Scenarios from Excel's Scenario Manager don't survive GridCraft:

- **Opening an Excel file drops them.** A workbook with three scenarios on its Assumptions sheet (`<scenarios>` in the sheet XML) opens with `data.scenarioManager` listing none. Saving then writes the file without them.
- **Scenarios added in GridCraft are invisible to Excel.** They are stored in a hidden defined name `_sc_scenarios` as a quoted JSON string. Excel's Scenario Manager shows nothing, and users see an odd name with a long string formula.

## Cause

- `crates/xlsx/src/sheet_read.rs` has no case for `<scenarios>`, and `sheet_write.rs` never writes it.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/whatif.rs` keeps the list in the hidden name (`load_scenarios` / `store_scenarios`), because the model had no place for scenarios.

## Fix

- **Model:** `Sheet::scenarios` (`Scenarios`: a list of `Scenario` plus `current`, `shown`, `result_cells`). Each scenario has name, changing cells with their values as typed, comment, user, `locked` and `hidden`, matching `CT_Scenarios` / `CT_Scenario`. It is serialized only when non-empty.
- **XLSX:**
  - The reader fills it from `<scenarios>`. Scenarios without changing cells are dropped and out-of-range indices are ignored. Input is bounded by Excel's limits: 32 changing cells, 1,000 scenarios.
  - The writer emits `<scenarios current show sqref>` after `<protectedRanges>` and before `<autoFilter>`, as the schema orders it.
- **Engine:** `load_scenarios` / `store_scenarios` now read and write the sheets' scenarios, so the `data.scenario*` commands and their JSON are unchanged.
  - Who added a scenario and its protection flags are kept; new scenarios are locked (Excel's "Prevent changes" default).
  - Show records the scenario as current and shown. Summary records its result cells, as Excel does.
  - Scenarios still in the legacy `_sc_scenarios` name (files saved by GridCraft so far) are read and move to their sheet on the next Show or change.

Data › What-If Analysis › Scenario Manager… does nothing visible: the menu item runs the `data.scenarioManager` query, and the result goes nowhere. title: UI: responsive ribbon — groups collapse into launcher dropdowns when narrow (#434)
author: edurbs
body:
Closes #434. Responsive ribbon: when a tab's groups exceed the card width, groups collapse into launcher buttons (rightmost first) whose dropdowns hold the group's controls; at full width nothing changes.

**Stacked on #456** (based on `prxnvt:pr/ui-kit` @ `15debc5`; I'll rebase onto `main` once it merges). Thanks @prxnvt for the coordination and for the `RibbonOverflow` per-frame sizing and `tests/ribbon_layout.rs` harness this builds directly on — and for confirming the intent this implements: *collapse groups first; scroll arrows only when the most compact layout still doesn't fit.*

## How it works

- Every tab's `sep()`-delimited regions are wrapped in `group(ui, name, hero, body)`; groups measure themselves per frame (same one-frame-lag pattern as `RibbonOverflow`), including separator/lead geometry, with the expanded width cached while collapsed.
- A pure `plan_for(measures, budget, current)` decides the collapse set per tab: expand-leftmost only with a 24 px hysteresis margin, then collapse-rightmost until the tab fits; groups that save no width are never collapsed. The plan is keyed per tab, so switching tabs never applies another tab's plan.
- A collapsed group renders a launcher (hero icon + translated group name) opening an `egui::Area` dropdown — an Area rather than `Popup::menu` because egui 0.36 has a single popup slot per viewport: with `Popup::menu`, any control inside the dropdown that opens its own popup (font/size combos, split arrows, galleries) would close the dropdown. With the Area form, nested control popups coexist (one submenu at a time, like Excel — egui's single slot). Pinned by `collapsed_group_dropdown_survives_nested_control_popups`.
- Dropdown open state is keyed by `(tab, group)` and forgotten on tab change, so no-click switches (control channel, commands, header/footer auto-switch) never resurrect a dropdown without a click.
- Below the collapse floor (≈ 540 px for Home) the tab still overflows and #456's scroll arrows remain the l…

title: XLSX: PivotCharts plot their cached points; deleted automatic titles stay off
author: neilcawse
body:
Excel-saved PivotCharts opened empty, or with a stray grand total bar, and charts whose automatic title had been deleted showed "Series1" as a title.

Excel often saves a PivotChart series with `<c:f>` formulas that only approximate its PivotTable. In a set of 11 Excel-saved fleet reports, every series of a combo PivotChart pointed at the PivotTable's corner cell (`Graph!$J$2`), and other charts used a block that takes in the grand total row (`Summary!$B$5:$B$13` for 8 cached points). Excel draws a PivotChart from its PivotTable, so the cached points are what it shows. GridCraft evaluated the formulas.

## What changed

Most changes are in `crates/xlsx/src/chart.rs`.

- **PivotChart series** (charts with `c:pivotSource`). When the cells a series' categories or values refer to don't hold their cached points (`numCache`, `strCache`, or the innermost level of a `multiLvlStrCache`), the series plots the cached points as array constants, and the cached name replaces the name reference. A literal name is saved as plain text with its doubled quotes read back as one (`Sales "East"`, not `Sales ""East""`), in chart and chartex parts alike (`literal_text`). Points missing from the cache become `#N/A` (numbers) or `""` (text), so later points keep their positions. The check needs every sheet's cells, so `read_chart` returns each PivotChart series' cache (`PivotSeriesCache`) and `plot_pivot_caches` runs in `read_xlsx` once the sheets are read. A reference stays live when it has one cell per point and each cell shows its point: numbers within rounding, text as is, and a number cache leaves out cells without a number. This also catches the corner-cell pattern when the PivotTable has one row item, where the corner cell and the cache both have one point. A `multiLvlStrRef` block of more than one level (`Graph!$A$4:$B$7` for 4 points) is compared by its innermost level only: the last column of a block with a row per point, or the last row of one with a column per point. title: XLSX: import grouped shapes and keep them as groups
author: neilcawse
body:
## Summary

Pictures, charts and shapes inside a grouped shape (`<xdr:grpSp>`) were dropped on open, with the warning "grouped shapes are not supported and were skipped". In Excel-saved reports this hides whole charts and banners. They are now imported at their group-transformed positions and the grouping is kept: a group saves back as one `grpSp`, and moving or deleting a member acts on the whole group, as in Excel. Tested on a set of 11 real Excel-saved fleet reports: in two of them, bar charts, text boxes, a logo banner and icons sit inside groups (one with a nested group).

## What changed

**Model** (`crates/model/src/group.rs`, new)
- `DrawingGroup` on `Sheet::groups`: id (from the same counter as other objects), name, its anchor, its child box (`chOff`/`chExt` in EMUs), its `flip` (`flipH`/`flipV`) and `rotation` (`rot`), the `rot` of each member that has one (`member_rotations`), and its members back to front as `DrawingRef` (`Chart`/`Image`/`Shape`/`Group`). Members stay ordinary charts, pictures and shapes in their sheet lists with resolved anchors, so drawing, hit-testing and everything else that reads anchors is unchanged.
- Helpers: `drawing_rect` (a group's box is the box around its members), `group_anchor`, `outer_group`, `group_contents`, `transform_group` (move/size a group and everything in it by one map), `set_group_anchor_mode`, `delete_group`. `drawing_rect_with` unions the boxes of the members `group_contents` lists, which skips repeats, so each nested group is visited once: a cycle, or a group listed twice, in hand-written JSON costs no more than the objects it holds. Nesting is capped at 64 levels.

title: Functions: COUNTIF family returns #VALUE! for criteria over 255 characters
author: neilcawse
body:
Excel returns `#VALUE!` for a text criterion longer than 255 UTF-16 code units in COUNTIF, SUMIF and AVERAGEIF, and in COUNTIFS, SUMIFS, AVERAGEIFS, MAXIFS and MINIFS when they have a single criteria pair. With two or more pairs, Excel instead matches the first 255 UTF-16 units of the criterion. GridCraft matched the whole long criterion in every case.

The calc oracle found this in an Excel-saved report. Active Engine Faults › Report!H28 is `=IF(COUNTIF($G$10:G28,G28)>1,0,1)`, where G28 is `=Data!A27&" "&Data!F27` with a cached value 268 characters long. Excel caches `#VALUE!`; GridCraft gave 1. The other COUNTIF cells in that column have criteria up to 213 characters, and their cached values are 0 or 1. So the limit applies to the evaluated criterion, not to the formula text.

## What changed

- `crates/functions/src/criteria.rs`: `MAX_CRITERION_UTF16_UNITS = 255`. `Criterion::parse_arg(&Value) -> Result<Criterion, CellError>` gives `#VALUE!` for text over 255 UTF-16 units. `Criterion::parse_arg_truncated(&Value) -> Criterion` parses only the first 255 UTF-16 units. Everything else goes to `parse` unchanged. For an array criterion, the first element is checked. Text of 255 bytes or fewer skips the count, and neither function allocates beyond what `parse` already does.
- Length is counted in UTF-16 code units, as Excel counts it: 😀 is 2 units, so `"a"×254 & "😀"` (255 characters, 256 units) is `#VALUE!` with one pair.
- When the 255-unit cut falls inside a surrogate pair (for example, 128 emoji), Excel's truncated criterion ends in half an emoji and matches nothing: SUMIFS gives 0, not the cell holding 127 emoji. GridCraft keeps the whole characters before the cut and marks the criterion as cut (`Operand::CutText`). No cell text can equal it, so `=` matches nothing and `<>` matches everything. For `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` it sorts just above the kept text. That comparison rule is an approximation, not checked in Excel, and only applies to comparison criteria over 255…

title: Bidirectional cell text: Arabic and Hebrew read right to left
author: mo2menmuhamed
body:
> Depends on #705, which it is built on so CI is green. Until that merges, this diff also shows its two commits; the changes here are the last two commits.

## Problem

Arabic in GridCraft displays wrongly, for example in this accounts sheet:

- numbers inside Arabic are reversed: `الرصيد في 28 فبراير` shows **82**
- Arabic words appear in the wrong order when a space falls back to another font face
- Arabic inside a Latin line, like `10102-customer-1111 - عبدالسلام`, can be misordered

egui 0.36 already shapes text with harfrust, so Arabic letters do join. What's missing is bidirectional layout. epaint cuts a line into runs by font face, shapes each run in a direction guessed from its script, then places the runs left to right in stored order. A right-to-left run is reversed as a whole, digits included, and multi-word Arabic ends up in the wrong order.

## Fix

**New `crates/ui-egui/src/bidi.rs`** runs the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (UAX #9) with `unicode-bidi` (pure Rust, wasm-safe) and gives egui each line as separate sections in display order:

- left-to-right runs as they are
- right-to-left runs as their Arabic/Hebrew chunks, each kept in reading order so the shaper turns and joins it, placed in reverse
- the spaces and punctuation between them reversed and mirrored (`(` ↔ `)`)
- Arabic-Indic digits as one section each, so the shaper doesn't reverse them as Arabic

Sections are pushed directly onto the `LayoutJob`: `LayoutJob::append` merges same-format sections back into one run, which undoes the reordering. The paragraph direction comes from the first strong character, like Excel's "Context" reading order.

**Where it's used:**

- **Grid cells** containing right-to-left text, wrapped cells included. Wrapped text is broken into lines in reading order first, then each line is reordered. Cells without right-to-left text take exactly the old code path.
- **General alignment** follows the reading order: text starting with an Arabic or Hebrew letter sits on t…

title: CSV: open Arabic (Windows-1256) and Cyrillic (Windows-1251) ANSI files
author: mo2menmuhamed
body:
> Depends on #705, which it is built on so CI is green. Until that merges, this diff also shows its two commits; the change here is the last commit.

## Problem

A CSV with no BOM that isn't valid UTF-8 was always decoded as Windows-1252. That is exactly what Excel writes as "CSV (Comma delimited)" on Arabic Windows, so those files opened as mojibake: `اسم` became `ÇÓã`. Russian files saved on Cyrillic Windows were garbled the same way.

## Fix

Excel reads such files in the system's ANSI code page, which the file doesn't record. New `guess_code_page` decides from the letter bytes (0xC0 and up):

1. **Western or not?** Western text puts its few accented letters inside words, next to ASCII letters ("café"). Arabic and Cyrillic words are runs of high bytes beside spaces, digits and punctuation. If fewer than a fifth of the letter bytes touch an ASCII letter, the text isn't Western.
2. **Arabic or Cyrillic?** The bytes that are Latin letters in Windows-1256 (`à â ç è é ê ë î ï ô ù û ü`) are among the most common Russian letters in Windows-1251 (`а в з и й к л о п ф щ ы ь`) and never appear in Arabic text. Over 15% of them means Cyrillic; otherwise Arabic.

Symbols below 0xC0 (`€ ° ±`) aren't counted, since they stand alone in any script; `Preis: 5 €` stays Western. Windows-1251 is decoded too, so Russian files aren't misread as Arabic.

`decode_ansi` holds full tables for both pages. Every byte maps to a char or U+FFFD, with no indexing and no panics.

## Screenshots

The same ANSI CSV files (encoded with Python's `cp1256` / `cp1251` codecs) opened on `main` and on this branch.

| | Before (`main`) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Arabic, Windows-1256 | ![pr3-arabic-cp1256-before.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mo2menmuhamed/gridcraft/pr-screenshots/pr3-arabic-cp1256-before.png) | ![pr3-arabic-cp1256-after.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mo2menmuhamed/gridcraft/pr-screenshots/pr3-arabic-cp1256-after.png) |

The buttons are now laid out first, right to left, and the field takes exactly what's left; the author line wraps too. On top of that the task pane is capped at half the window, so no content can cover the sheet again. Half is my pick, happy to switch.

title: XLSX: read, evaluate and write Excel 2010 conditional formats
author: neilcawse
body:
Conditional formats in the worksheet's Excel 2010 `x14:conditionalFormattings` extension (MS-XLSX [2.4.6](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-xlsx/e5876d4c-5362-497f-bd1a-b6de4604d11c)) were skipped on open, with the warning "some Excel 2010 conditional format extensions were skipped".

A x14 rule holds its formulas in `xm:f` elements and its format in an inline `x14:dxf`, not a `dxfId`. In a set of fleet reports, one report (`watchdog-report.xlsx`) keeps two `cellIs equal 'Vehicle Range'!$A$8`-style rules there, which grey out a status column. That file was saved by **LibreOffice 25.2** (`docProps/app.xml`: `<Application>LibreOffice/25.2.2.1…`), not Excel; the other ten reports are Excel-saved and have no x14 conditional formats. GridCraft dropped the two rules, so the column showed no formatting, and a save lost them for good.

**What MS-XLSX says.** [2.6.27 CT_CfRule](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-xlsx/025ea6e4-ad42-43ea-a016-16f4e4688ac8) restricts the `xm:f` formulas of a x14 rule: they MUST NOT use `book-prefix`, `bang-reference`, `sheet-range-reference` (3-D spans), `structure-reference` (among others) or match `single-sheet-area`. A `single-sheet-reference` such as `'Vehicle Range'!$A$8` is allowed. The spec does not say that Excel keeps cross-sheet rules in the extension, or that the main section can't hold them. Writing them in the extension follows the LibreOffice-saved file; where Excel itself puts them is unverified.

## What changed

- **Read** (`crates/xlsx/src/sheet_read.rs`). `read_x14_cf` reads these x14 rule kinds as ordinary `CondFormat`s: `cellIs` (every operator, with one or two formulas), `expression`, `containsBlanks`/`notContainsBlanks`, `containsErrors`/`notContainsErrors`, `duplicateValues`/`uniqueValues`, `top10`, `aboveAverage` and `timePeriod`. Each rule keeps its `priority` (shared with the main-section rules, so the order interleaves), `stopIfTrue`, its `xm:sqref` ranges an…

title: PivotTables: values on rows (Σ Values in Rows, dataOnRows)
author: neilcawse
body:
PivotTables with "values on rows" (Excel's `dataOnRows`, the Σ Values field in the Rows area) opened with the warning `values on rows are shown on columns`. GridCraft always put the value fields across columns, and saving dropped the setting.

## Summary

When a PivotTable has two or more value fields, the Σ Values pseudo-field can now sit in Rows as well as Columns, at any position among the row fields. In Columns it stays after the last column field, as before. It is laid out the way Excel does it in compact, outline and tabular form, can be moved with `pivot.moveField` and the PivotTable Fields pane, and is kept through an XLSX save.

## What changed

- **Model** (`crates/model/src/features.rs`). `PivotTable` gets `values_on_rows: bool` and `values_position: Option<usize>`, the index of Σ Values among the row fields (`None` means after the last). It is only used with values on rows: in Columns, Σ Values always comes after the last column field. Both default to the old behaviour (Columns, last) and are `#[serde(default)]` through the struct.
- **Engine layout** (`crates/engine/src/pivot.rs`). With values on rows, Σ Values counts as a row level:
  - Each value field becomes a row item at that level ("Sum of Sales", "Sum of Units"). Below it come the remaining row fields; innermost, the item itself holds the value.
  - An item with Σ Values below it gets one subtotal line per value field ("East Sum of Sales", "East Sum of Units"), below its group. Grand totals are one line per value field ("Total Sum of Sales"). With only Σ Values in Rows there is no grand total, because the value items already are the totals.
  - Compact indents the Σ Values level like any row field. Outline and tabular give it its own column, headed "Values". Tabular starts the first value item on its parent's row.
  - There is one data column per column item, and each line takes the value field it names. With no column field, the header above that one data column reads "Total", as Excel saves it.…

title: PivotTables: slicers from XLSX files are shown, filter their PivotTables and are saved
author: neilcawse
body:
PivotTable slicers in Excel files were dropped on open with the warning "an embedded object (SmartArt, OLE...) was skipped", and were lost on save.

An Excel 2010+ PivotTable slicer is spread over several parts: a drawing frame (`sle:slicer` inside `mc:AlternateContent`, with a fallback text shape for older readers), a slicer part (`xl/slicers/slicerN.xml`: caption, columns, style, button height), a slicer cache (`xl/slicerCaches/slicerCacheN.xml`: source field, connected PivotTables, and tabular items with their selected flags), plus the workbook `x14:slicerCaches` and sheet `x14:slicerList` ext entries. GridCraft only read the drawing, and treated the frame as an unknown embedded object.

## What changed

- **Model** (`crates/model/src/features.rs`). `Slicer` now has a `source: SlicerSource` enum: `Table { table, column, selected }` (the existing table slicer) or `Pivot { pivots, field, sort, cross_filter, show_missing }`. It also gains `name`, `style` and `row_height`. A pivot slicer stores no selection of its own: the selection is each connected PivotTable's `PivotFilter` on the field, which is what Excel stores as hidden pivot items, so the two always agree. `PivotFilter` gains `hidden`, for a field the PivotTable filters without showing a report filter cell (a slicer on a field outside Rows and Columns). It also gains `date_group`: the date grouping its items are in when no Rows/Columns field implies it. In Excel the grouping belongs to the cache field (ECMA-376 §18.10.1.33), so a Date field grouped by months keeps its months when it is in no area, and a filter on a field grouped at several levels names the level it filters. `PivotTable::field_group` gives the grouping of a field's base cache field (the finest level).
- **Import** (new `crates/xlsx/src/slicer.rs`, hooks in `drawing.rs`, `sheet_read.rs`, `read.rs`, `pivot.rs`). The frame is taken from the `a14` choice, not the fallback. The slicer part and the slicer cache come from the sheet and workbook ext l…

title: cell.set / set_cell: accept a number for `input` (#697)
author: dantebertuzzi
body:
Fixes #697.

## Problem
`cell.set` documents `input` as `"text, number or =formula"`, and MCP `set_cell` says "number, text or =formula", but only a string was read for `input`:

- engine: `str_param(p, "input")` is `None` for a JSON number, and only the `value` alias fell back to `json_to_input`, so `{"input": 123.5}` errored with "missing `input`" on `main` (and silently cleared the cell on 0.5.0);
- MCP: the schema typed `input` as `string`, so `{"input": 42.5}` was rejected.

## Fix
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs`: resolve `input`, then `value`, through the same `json_to_input` converter (numbers, booleans, strings). A call with neither key still returns the existing error.
- `crates/mcp/src/tools.rs`: `set_cell.input` is typed `["string", "number", "boolean"]`, matching its description.

## Tests
- `cmd::edit::tests::cell_set_takes_numbers_for_input_and_value`: number via `input`, number via `value`, boolean, a formula over the numeric cells, and the missing-input error.
- `crates/mcp/src/tests.rs` `basic_tools`: `set_cell` with a numeric `input` round-trips through `get_cell`.

`cargo test -p gridcraft-engine -p gridcraft-mcp` and `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-engine -p gridcraft-mcp --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass locally. I did not run the full `cargo xtask ci` (wasm target).

title: Arabic (العربية) UI translation: language switching + font fallback
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
An `ar.rs` catalog (1,268 entries) for the whole interface — ribbon tabs, backstage pages, menus, dialogs and status messages, with the `context|label` rows the other catalogs use — written with the spreadsheet vocabulary Arabic Excel users know (ورقة العمل، تجميد الأجزاء، الصفحة الرئيسية، تخطيط الصفحة…).

- **Registry** — `Language::Ar` in the enum, `ALL`, `name`, `code`, `from_tag` (every `ar-*` locale resolves) and `tr()`, plus the `app.language.arabic` command and its row in `control.rs`.
- **Fonts** — the Arabic chain (Segoe UI, Tahoma, Traditional Arabic on Windows; Geeza Pro on macOS; Noto Sans Arabic and friends on Linux) appended to the UI families, so a system face always paints Arabic.

I can't build the Rust here, so the catalog was validated against the repo's invariants (the sorted-keyed lookups, placeholder parity, no duplicate keys) and the brace balance of every touched file.

شكراً لمراجعتكم — أتمنى أن تكون الإضافة مفيدة لمستخدمي العربية.

No layout mirroring in this PR: egui 0.36 has no global direction switch and no bidi reordering, so the shell still lays out left-to-right and the words of an Arabic label come out in reverse order until a bidi pass (the approach discussed in vectorcraft#1202) lands. I kept this PR to the catalog, the language switch and the fonts rather than pretend at mirroring an API that doesn't exist.

title: PivotTables: refresh keeps sort by value, captions, item order and layout settings
author: neilcawse
body:
Refreshing a PivotTable read from an Excel file gave a different report from the one Excel shows. Items came out sorted by label when the file sorts them by a value, headers read "Row Labels", "Values" and the source column names instead of the file's captions, renamed items lost their names, manually ordered columns were re-sorted, and per-field subtotal and label settings were dropped. The PivotTable definition stores all of these settings, but GridCraft didn't read them, or read them and didn't apply them.

## What changed

The model changes are in `crates/model/src/features.rs`, the layout changes in `crates/engine/src/pivot.rs` and the XLSX read/write in `crates/xlsx/src/pivot.rs`. Every new field is `#[serde(default)]`.

- **Sort by a value field.** `PivotField.sort_by: Option<String>` (a value field's caption) sorts the items by that value field in the `sort` direction, within each parent item, with subtotals. It is read from `<autoSortScope>` when the scope refers to the Values field (`field="4294967294"`) and data item n, and written back the same way. `pivot.sort` takes `by: "Sum of Sales"` (a caption or a source field in the Values area). Renaming the value field with `pivot.valueSettings` keeps the sort.
- **Sort scope.** `PivotField.sort_scope: Vec<PivotScopeItem>` (source column, date grouping, item label) says where the sort takes its values: Excel's "sort by the values in the Apples column" adds a reference to an item of a field on the other axis to the `<autoSortScope>`. It is read, written back (as the index into that field's `<items>`) and used by the engine, which used to sort by the grand total. Entries name their field by source column *and* date grouping, so Years and Quarters grouped from one date column stay apart. The engine and the writer resolve a scope the same way: the other axis's fields outer first, up to the first one it doesn't name; a scope naming an item that's no longer there sorts by the grand total, and is saved as a sort by th…

title: Spelling in the interface language with installed Hunspell dictionaries (craft-proof)
author: brzuchal
body:
## Summary

GridCraft's Spelling (F7) checks in the interface language, using the Hunspell dictionary installed for it. Today it only reads `/usr/share/dict/words` (English, and nothing on Windows or the web), and skips every word with a non-ASCII letter.

> **Draft, depends on two open PRs:**
> - https://github.com/storytold/craft-libs/pull/31 — the shared `craft-proof` crate (https://github.com/storytold/craft-libs/issues/30). It is pinned here to the #31 commit in my fork (`brzuchal/craft-libs@20dfbeb`) and will be repinned to `storytold/craft-libs` when #31 merges.
> - https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/pull/650 — the Polish interface (`Language::Pl`). This branch is based on it, so its commits show here until it merges; the new commit is the last one.

## What changes

- `review.spelling` takes `lang` (a BCP 47 tag). With no `lang`, or an `en` tag, it keeps the system word list exactly as before.
- Any other language checks against the installed Hunspell pair (`pl_PL.aff`/`.dic`, then `pl`), found with `craft_proof::hunspell::Search::for_app("GridCraft")`:
  - the `spelling::set_dictionary_dir` setting;
  - `GRIDCRAFT_DICTIONARIES`;
  - `%LOCALAPPDATA%\GridCraft\dictionaries`;
  - OS packages, Homebrew and LibreOffice.
  Loaded dictionaries are cached per language.
- Suggestions are dictionary words one edit away, using the dictionary's `TRY` letters, with the word's capitalisation kept. The user dictionary applies in every language.
- A language with no installed dictionary returns an error ("No pl-PL spelling dictionary is installed…") rather than marking every word as an English misspelling.
- The Spelling dialog passes the interface language through the new `Language::spelling_tag()` (`pl-PL`, `pt-BR`, `de-DE`, `es-ES`, `fr-FR`, `ru-RU`, `cs-CZ`). English, Chinese, Japanese and Korean stay on the English word list.

GridCraft has no per-cell language, so the interface language is the proxy.

title: Numfmt: a negative number that rounds to zero shows no minus sign
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #729.

`format_number` put the `-` in front of every negative number formatted by the first section, even when the rounded digits were all zero, so `-0.0033` in `0.00` came out as `-0.00` (Excel: `0.00`). `render_number` now reports whether every digit it shows is zero, and the sign is skipped in that case. Only the default-negative path changes: a format with its own negative section (`0.00;(0.00)`, `0.00;-0.00;"zero"`) is untouched, and scientific formats keep the sign since their mantissa is never all zeros. Fraction formats are left as they were. The old `f("0.0", -0.04) == "-0.0"` assertion in `numbers` expected the bug, so it now expects `0.0`.

Validation:
- `negative_rounding_to_zero_drops_the_sign` (the issue's Excel table) and the two `TEXT()` cases in `text_fn`: fail on main (`-0.00`, `-0`), pass here
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-numfmt --lib tests::`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-numfmt --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: macOS: register the Window menu as NSApp's windowsMenu, so the tiling shortcuts work
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #716.

The native menu bar had a Window menu, but it was never registered as `NSApp.windowsMenu`. That's the menu macOS fills with Move & Resize, Fill, Center and the window list, and the system tiling shortcuts (Fn+Ctrl+arrows, Fn+F) act through those items: with no windows menu there was nothing for them to hit. The install now calls muda's `set_as_windows_menu_for_nsapp()` on the Window submenu after `init_for_nsapp()`, the same way PhotoCraft does in its `mac_menu.rs`.

Adds `apps/gridcraft/tests/mac_menu_appkit.rs` (`harness = false`, runs on the main thread like PhotoCraft's): it installs the real menu and reads NSApp back. It needs `objc2`/`objc2-app-kit` as macOS dev-dependencies, pinned to the versions already in Cargo.lock (the lock only gains two dependency lines).

Validation:
- `cargo test -p gridcraft --test mac_menu_appkit`: fails on main (`windowsMenu()` is `None`), passes here; fails again with the call removed
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: EDATE and EOMONTH: serial 0 is day 0 and February 1900 has 28 days
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #734.

EDATE clamped the start day up to 1, so serial 0 (an empty date cell) became 1 January 1900 instead of 0 January, and both EDATE and EOMONTH took month lengths from the sheet's calendar, where February 1900 has the Lotus 29th. Excel's EDATE and EOMONTH keep day 0 and end February 1900 on the 28th. Now EDATE keeps the day as read and both use the real month lengths (`days_in_month`). Serial 60 still reads as 29 February, so `EDATE(60,1)` stays 29 March, and DATE, DAY and the parser keep the leap day from #124. This changes four assertions added with #124 that expected 60 at the end of February 1900; they now expect 59, matching the Excel values in the issue.

Validation:
- `date::tests::edate_eomonth_early_1900` (the table from the issue): fails on main (`EDATE(0,0)` gives 1, expected 0), passes here
- `date::tests::fictitious_1900_02_29`: fails on main (`EOMONTH(DATE(1900,1,15),1)` gives 60, expected 59), passes here
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-functions --lib date::`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-functions --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: ROMAN: forms 2 and 3 subtract IC, XM and VM like Excel
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #733.

`roman_tokens` modelled each form as one maximum ratio between the subtracted numeral and the larger one (10, 20, 50, 100, 1000). Excel's forms don't fit a single ratio: form 2 writes `IC` and `XM` (ratio 100) but not `VD` (also 100), and form 3 writes `VM` (200) but not `ID`. They do fit two limits, one for I/X/C and one for V/L, with each form widening one of them in turn: I/X/C allow 10, 10, 100, 100, 1000 and V/L allow none, 20, 20, 200, 200. That's what the table is now. Forms 0, 1 and 4 come out the same as before.

I dumped `ROMAN(n, form)` for all 19,995 inputs before and after: exactly the 92 cases from the issue change (72 in form 2, 20 in form 3), nothing else does.

Validation:
- `math::tests::roman_forms_two_and_three_match_excel` (the 92 cases from the issue, plus neighbours like `ROMAN(495,2)` = `XDV` and `ROMAN(495,3)` = `VD`): fails on main (`ROMAN(99,2)` gives `VCIV`, expected `IC`), passes here
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-functions --lib math::tests`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-functions --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: functions: MODE skips typed text and logical arguments
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #736.

`mode_numbers` returned `#VALUE!` for any text argument typed into the formula and coerced typed `TRUE`/`FALSE` to numbers. Excel skips both, so MODE, MODE.SNGL and MODE.MULT now ignore text and logical scalar arguments (typed or referenced) and still propagate errors left to right. A single-cell reference to a blank cell stays `#VALUE!`, which matches Excel's cached result for `MODE(B9,2,D7)` in POI's FormulaEvalTestData.xls.

The `#VALUE!` cases in `mode_scalar_arguments` came from that workbook's "EXPECTED VALUE" row. The values Excel actually cached in the formula row above it are `#N/A` for `MODE(C9,E16,"1",B8)` and `MODE(B8,"1",2,3)`, and `#DIV/0!` for the `"1",1,#DIV/0!,2,3` case, which agrees with the Excel 365 table in the issue. I updated those three cases to match.

Validation:
- `stat::tests::mode_skips_typed_text_and_logicals` (the issue's table, for MODE, MODE.SNGL and MODE.MULT): fails on main (`=MODE(1,1,"x")` gives `#VALUE!`), passes here
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-functions --lib stat::`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-functions --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: XLS: a FORMAT record shorter than its character count keeps the characters it holds
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #731.

The FORMAT arm in `globals()` read the code with `Cursor::string()`, which asks for `cch` characters and fails when the record ends first; the error went all the way up and the workbook didn't open. A FORMAT record never needs a `Continue` (255 characters at most), so when `cch` is larger than what the record holds the reader now keeps the characters that are there, adds one warning to the report, and carries on. For the govdocs file in the issue that gives exactly the 50-character code of format 42. I kept the characters rather than dropping the format so cells keep the format Excel shows; happy to switch to skipping the record (General) if you prefer. The broader "tolerate other optional records" idea from the issue is left out to keep this small.

Validation:
- `xls_tests::a_format_shorter_than_its_count_keeps_its_characters`: fails on main (`XLS: record is shorter than its contents`), passes here; the bad FORMAT sits before a good one and both formats, plus the cell values, are checked
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-xlsx --lib xls_tests`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-xlsx --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: XLS import: read the calculation settings (iteration, mode, precision as displayed)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #724.

The BIFF8 reader skipped the calculation-settings records, so `wb.calc` stayed at the defaults and a workbook saved with iterative calculation on opened with it off: every cell in a circular reference showed `#CIRC!`. CalcMode (0x000D), CalcCount (0x000C), CalcIter (0x0011) and CalcDelta (0x0010) repeat in every worksheet substream; the reader now collects them per sheet and applies the first worksheet's values to `wb.calc`. CalcPrecision (0x000E) sits in the globals and sets `precision_as_displayed`. These are the same fields the .xlsx reader fills from `<calcPr calcMode iterate iterateCount iterateDelta fullPrecision>`, and counts and deltas go through `set_max_iterations` / `set_max_change`, so out-of-range values are clamped the same way. Taking the first worksheet (rather than the active one) is a choice; happy to switch.

Validation:
- `xls_tests::reads_iterative_calculation_settings`: fails on main (`wb.calc.iterative` is false), passes here. It also checks manual mode from CalcMode and precision as displayed from CalcPrecision, and removing either arm makes it fail. The second sheet carries no calc records, so a "last sheet wins" reading fails it too
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-xlsx --lib xls`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-xlsx --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
