title: macOS: the title bar carries the document's file icon; dragging it drags the file out
author: jellologic
body:
Fixes #1169.

Native macOS document windows carry their file: the title bar shows the file's icon, dragging it out of the window drags the file (into Finder, an e-mail, a chat), and the close button wears the edited dot while there are unsaved changes. GridCraft had none of the three: it paints its own title bar, and winit 0.30 neither sets the represented filename nor offers a drag session. This adds all three on macOS; Windows, Linux, BSD and the web are untouched.

The title bar now draws the active document's file icon — the file's real Finder icon, fetched through NSWorkspace and cached as a texture — centred, immediately left of the title, Excel's arrangement. Dragging it starts a native `NSDraggingSession` with the file URL, so drop targets accept the file itself; the drag image is the file's icon. The edited dot is winit's safe `set_document_edited`. AppKit's own proxy icon was considered first (an empty title plus a represented filename shows the icon alone — verified) but AppKit draws it after the traffic lights, exactly where the Quick Access Toolbar lives, so the painted-icon route keeps the toolbar where it is.

While measuring the icon spacing I re-measured the traffic lights themselves (#170): on current macOS they are 13 pt wide on a 23 pt pitch starting 9 pt in, not the 12 / 20 / 10 the QAT offset assumed — the old numbers left a hair between the lights and AutoSave. The constants now match the measured geometry, which the existing lights test still derives.

The AppKit interop lives in the new `gridcraft-macos-window` (L0 leaf, registered in the layering table): Objective-C messaging needs `unsafe`, which the workspace forbids elsewhere — the same reasoning as `fmv-macos-events` (#69), with the `unsafe` confined to a few documented message sends. An app that keeps a native title bar (EffectCraft and SoundCraft today) would use the crate's `set_represented_filename` instead; the crate carries both strategies deliberately, and the eleven sibling apps…

title: Conditional formatting: text rules take wildcards and skip error values
author: iluebbe
body:
Fixes #1161 and #1162: two ways the text rules of conditional formatting differed from Excel.

## Problem

Measured in Excel for Microsoft 365 against GridCraft (`main` 84acf62):

- **Wildcards (#1161).** Excel saves "Text that Contains" as `NOT(ISERROR(SEARCH("a*c",A1)))`, so `*` matches any run of characters, `?` one character and `~` makes the next one literal. GridCraft searched literally: "contains `a*c`" formatted only a cell holding `a*c`, where Excel also formats abc, ABC, Abcdef, xabc, a?c and abxc. "Begins with" and "Ends with" are literal in Excel too, and stay so.
- **Error values (#1162).** GridCraft searched an error's text, so `#N/A` "contained" `a` and "began with" `#`. In Excel, an error never contains, begins or ends with anything, and always "does not contain". Excel's rule formulas fail on an error value.

## Fix

`crates/engine/src/cf.rs`:
- **Wildcards:** "Text that Contains" and "does not contain" search like `SEARCH`, case-insensitively, with the engine's existing `*`/`?`/`~` matcher (`cmd::edit::wildcard`, also used by Find and the criteria commands).
- **Errors:** an error value never matches "contains", "begins with" or "ends with", and always matches "does not contain".

`docs/gaps.md` gets §25, a list of what the measurement against Excel found (#1158–#1165).

## Testing

- `text_that_contains_takes_wildcards`: `a*c`, `a?c`, `a~*c`, "does not contain `a*c`" and "begins with `a*`" over abc, ABC, xabc, abxc, a*c, a?c and ab. Expected values are as measured in Excel; `a~*c` follows `SEARCH`'s documented escape.
- `text_rules_on_error_values`: `=NA()`, `=1/0` and `abc` under contains / begins with / ends with / does not contain, as measured in Excel.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers and wasm pass.
  - `parity` and `keytips --check` report their generated files out of date on this Windows checkout (`core.autocrlf`).
  - Regenerating them changes only line endings: `git diff` is empty, as on `main`.

title: fix(edit): paste, Ctrl+Enter, Fill and Copy skip rows a filter hides (#1101)
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary

Pasting a single copied cell or row over a filtered selection, Ctrl+Enter, and Fill Down/Up/Right/Left now skip the rows an applied filter hides, as Excel does. Before this, every hidden row in the selection was overwritten (#1101). Copying a filtered range now takes only the rows showing, so pasting it inside GridCraft no longer brings the hidden rows back.

Excel's rule, measured in Excel for Microsoft 365 via COM:

| Action over a filtered selection | Excel | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paste one cell / one row | showing rows only | all rows | showing rows only |
| Paste a taller block | straight down, hidden rows included | same | same |
| Ctrl+Enter | showing rows only | all rows | showing rows only |
| Fill Down / Up / Right | showing rows only | all rows | showing rows only |
| Rows hidden by hand (no filter) | written | written | written |

title: fix: extend formula references with Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+arrows in the editor
author: paulohenriquex
body:
## What

When editing a formula (in the cell or in the formula bar), Command+Shift+arrow on macOS and Ctrl+Shift+arrow on any platform did not extend the pointed reference. They either moved the text caret or did nothing, because the editor only consumed Shift+arrow events.

Additionally, the formula bar explicitly disabled pointing altogether (`!ed.from_formula_bar`), so not even plain Shift+arrow worked there.

## Why

- The shared editor widget only matched `Modifiers::NONE` and `Modifiers::SHIFT`, so any combination with Command or Ctrl fell through to the TextEdit's default behaviour.
- The formula-bar branch of the arrow handling had a `!ed.from_formula_bar` guard that skipped pointing entirely.

## How

- Capture `modifiers.command || modifiers.ctrl` alongside `modifiers.shift` when reading arrow key state.
- Consume `COMMAND|SHIFT` and `CTRL|SHIFT` variants so the events do not slip through to the TextEdit.
- Remove the `!ed.from_formula_bar` guard so pointing works in both editors.
- Pass a `jump` flag into `grid::point_move` and use the engine's `selection::jump` when set, so Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+arrow jumps to the edge of the data region like the grid does outside editing.

## Testing

- `cargo check -p gridcraft-ui-egui` passes.
- Manually tested in the running app on macOS:
  - In-cell editor: Cmd+Shift+arrow and Ctrl+Shift+arrow now extend the reference to the edge of the data region.
  - Formula bar: Shift+arrow, Cmd+Shift+arrow and Ctrl+Shift+arrow all extend the reference (previously nothing happened).
  - Plain Shift+arrow still extends cell by cell.
  - No regression in F4 anchor cycling, Enter/Esc/Tab handling, or grid-level Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+arrow selection.

title: fix(ui): menu items highlight under the pointer (#1174)
author: richard1912
body:
Fixes #1174.

The cell and header right-click menus, the ribbon dropdown menus (`menu_items`) and the data validation pick list drew their items with `Button::frame(false)`, which turns the background off in every state, hover included, so nothing showed which item a click would run. `frame_when_inactive(false)` keeps the items flat at rest and draws the theme's hover background under the pointer, as Excel's menus do. Four one-word changes in `grid.rs` and `ribbon.rs`.

![Before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/richard1912/gridcraft/issue-assets-dialogs/issue-assets/menus/menu_before_after.png)

## Testing
- `menu_hover.rs`: right-clicks a cell and a column header, checks that Copy has no background, moves the pointer onto it and checks that a rect in the hovered-widget colour is painted under it. Both tests fail on main ("Copy is highlighted under the pointer") and pass here.

title: Prompt to save changes before closing window
author: Osaym
body:
Closes #1172

### Summary
When closing GridCraft with unsaved workbooks or active cell/text-box edits, GridCraft previously exited immediately without prompting the user to save changes. Additionally, closing the last open workbook via `Cmd+W` or choosing "Don't Save" on the close prompt cleared the screen to a new blank workbook rather than closing the window.

### Changes
1. **Window Close & Dirty Tracking** (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`):
   - Added `pub quit_confirmed: bool` and `SheetApp::close_requested(&mut self) -> bool`.
   - Active in-progress cell or text-box edits are committed before checking dirty status so changes typed right before closing are preserved.
   - If workbooks are dirty and quit has not been confirmed, cancels close and opens the `saveChanges` dialog with `closingWindow: true`.
   - Closing the last open workbook on desktop (`self.session.active().is_none()`) confirms quit and closes the window instead of respawning a blank workbook.

2. **Save Changes Dialog Actions** (`crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`):
   - **Save** (or Enter): Commits edit, saves document, closes it, and prompts for any remaining dirty workbooks before closing the window.
   - **Don't Save**: Closes the document with `force: true`; prompts for remaining dirty documents if any, or closes the window if all are handled.
   - **Cancel** (or Escape): Closes the dialog and aborts closing, leaving the window and unsaved workbooks open.

3. **Eframe Logic** (`apps/gridcraft/src/main.rs`):
   - Wires `close_requested()` check into eframe app logic to cancel window close requests until confirmed.

4. **Tests** (`crates/ui-egui/tests/window_close.rs`):
   - Added 9 tests covering clean close, dirty prompt, in-progress cell edit commitment, Cancel, Don't Save, Save, multiple dirty workbooks, and `Cmd+W` closing behavior.

title: Draw: typed ink, Excel InkML and Draw with Trackpad (Force Touch)
author: rustycawk
body:
Brings the Draw tab closer to Excel's. Ink gets a typed model with pressure, Excel's InkML file format, editable pens and erasers, and **Draw with Trackpad** with Force Touch pressure on macOS.

### What changes for users

- **Pens:** an editable pen gallery (pen, pencil, highlighter) where each pen has a colour, a width and an optional effect (rainbow, galaxy, gold…). Pens can be added and removed.

- **Stroke width:** width follows pressure when the input reports it, and drawing speed otherwise.

- **Draw with Trackpad:** a floating canvas over the sheet. One finger draws, two fingers move the canvas, and any key exits.
  - On macOS, a light touch draws the thinnest line; clicking the pad down and pressing harder thickens it. It uses `NSPressureBehavior.primaryGeneric`, so there is no force click or Look Up.

title: Scripts with logic: Rhai with an Office Scripts-shaped object model, Code Editor and Automate tab
author: Herr-Enklo
body:
Scripts with real logic for GridCraft (gaps.md §21). Today a "script" is a recorded list of commands; this adds a scripting language with an object model, a Code Editor and Excel 365's Automate tab layout.

> **Two decisions for the maintainers.**
> 1. **Language.** gaps.md §21 leaves the language to you. This PR proposes [Rhai](https://rhai.rs): pure Rust, builds for wasm32, sandboxable. The docs describe it as a proposal.
> 2. **One new licence.** Rhai depends on `smartstring` (MPL-2.0, used unmodified). It would be the workspace's first MPL dependency. This is recorded in `docs/decisions.md`.

## Object model
- Names follow Excel's documented Office Scripts API, so existing knowledge carries over:

  ```rhai
  fn main(workbook) {
      let sheet = workbook.getActiveWorksheet();
      sheet.getRange("A1:B3").setValues([["Month", "Sales"], ["Jan", 120], ["Feb", 140]]);
      sheet.getRange("A1:B1").getFormat().getFont().setBold(true);
      run("home.fillColor", #{range: "A1:B1", color: "#FFFF00"});   // any GridCraft command
      console.log("done");
  }
  ```

- Workbook, Worksheet, Range (values, formulas, texts, number formats, offset/resize, used range, surrounding region), formats (font, fill, alignment, sizes, autofit) and NamedItem are covered.
- `run(id, params)` reaches every command.
- Every write goes through `Session::execute`, so protection, recalculation and the journal apply. One run is one undo step ("Run Script"), including a run that fails partway.

## Sandbox
- Limits on operations, time, call depth, expression depth and string/array/map size. A runaway loop or deep recursion ends with an error instead of freezing.
- Native runs use a helper thread with a large stack. The browser gets smaller limits.
- Rhai is built with `no_time`, `no_module` and `no_closure`, and `eval` is off.
- Scripts can't reach files: `file.*` commands and any `path`/`url` param are refused unless the CLI's `--allow-files` is given.
- `automate.*` is refused inside scrip…

title: Conditional formatting: show a rule's number format
author: iluebbe
body:
Fixes #1163: GridCraft didn't show a conditional format's number format.

## Problem

A rule can set a number format in three ways:
- Format › Number in Excel's rule dialog;
- `numFmt` in the rule's `dxf`;
- `"style": {"num_fmt": "0.00"}` in `home.conditionalFormat`.

GridCraft read the format and `CfCache::look` returned it. The grid's `look` and the print/PDF path's `cell_look` merged only the rule's fill, font and borders, though, so the cell kept its own format.

Example: an Excel file with the rule "greater than 2" and the number format `#,000` shows `003` in Excel and `3` in GridCraft.

## Fix

- `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs` (`look`, which the Page Layout view also paints with) and `crates/engine/src/cmd/print.rs` (`cell_look`) take the rule's `num_fmt` when it isn't `General`. In a differential style, `General` means "not set"; `cf::layer_under` already treats it that way.
- For cells that aren't General, print's `draw_text` formatted the text with the cell's own style again (`display::cell_text`). It now formats with the look's code, through the new `display::value_text_as`. `value_text` calls `value_text_as`, so CSV/Text output is unchanged.

## Testing

- `a_rules_number_format_is_shown` (ui-egui, `grid.rs`): the rule's code replaces the cell's only where the rule matches.
- `pdf_shows_a_rules_number_format` (engine, `print.rs`): the PDF shows `3.00` for the matching cell and `1` for the other one. Before the `draw_text` change it showed `3`.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers and wasm pass.
  - `parity` and `keytips` report their generated files out of date on this Windows checkout (`core.autocrlf`).
  - Regenerating them changes only line endings: `git diff` is empty, as on `main`.

title: Conditional formatting: icon thresholds with ">" (gte="0")
author: iluebbe
body:
Fixes #1160: icon set thresholds with ">" were evaluated as ">=".

## Problem

In Excel, each icon threshold is ">=" (the default) or ">". The file stores ">" as `gte="0"` on the threshold's `cfvo`. GridCraft ignored `gte`, so a value exactly on a ">" threshold got the next higher icon. Saving the file then dropped the `gte`.

Measured in Excel for Microsoft 365, 3 Traffic Lights over 0…10:

| Thresholds | Value | Excel | GridCraft before | GridCraft now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number > 3, > 6 | 3 | red | yellow | red |
| | 6 | yellow | green | yellow |
| Percent > 30, > 70 | 3 | red | yellow | red |
| | 7 | yellow | green | yellow |

## Fix

- **Model:** `CfRule::IconSet` gets `greater: Vec<bool>`, one flag per threshold (same index as `thresholds`). It has a serde default, and an empty list means every threshold is ">=", so existing rules and saved state are unchanged.
- **XLSX:**
  - the reader takes `gte` from each `cfvo`;
  - the writer writes `gte="0"` where a flag is set, also when the lower bound is left out and gets prepended.
- **Evaluation** (`cf.rs`): compares with `>` where the flag is set.
- **Command:** `home.conditionalFormat` takes icon thresholds, which it had no parameter for: `{"type": "iconSet", "thresholds": [{"type": "num", "value": 3, "operator": ">"}, …]}`. List them from the lowest up, one per icon after the first; one per icon with the lower bound first, as in the file, works too.

## Testing

- `icon_thresholds_with_greater_than` (engine): the table above, plus ">=" for comparison, through the command.
- `icon_set_greater_than_thresholds_roundtrip` (xlsx): `gte="0"` is written on the right `cfvo` and read back.
- `full_roundtrip`: its icon set now carries ">" thresholds and still compares equal.
- **Excel:** a file this branch wrote with `> 3` and `> 6` opens with `IconCriteria(2..3).Operator = xlGreater`.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers and wasm pass.
  - `parity` and `keytips` report their generated files out of …

title: Grid: an armed Format Painter pastes onto the next cells clicked or dragged
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1211.

The ribbon button was fine: a click picked up the selection's format and the button showed as pressed. The missing half was on the grid side. `edit.formatPainter` only pastes when it is called with `{apply: range}`, and nothing in the UI ever made that call, so the next click on a cell just selected it and the painter stayed armed with nothing happening. The grid now makes that call when a cell selection is released (click or drag), with the cells just selected as the target. A single-click painter turns itself off afterwards and a double-clicked one stays on, both handled by the existing command. Releases in formula point mode are skipped, because that mode also uses the Select drag. The button also gets an accessibility label and toggled state, like Paste and Borders already have, so the test can find it.

Clicks on row or column headers don't paint yet (they use a different drag). Happy to add that here or in a follow-up.

- `format_painter::ribbon_button_picks_up_the_format_and_a_click_on_a_cell_pastes_it` (kittest: bold + fill on A1, click the ribbon button, click C3): fails on main (C3 keeps the default style), passes here

title: File: Save a Copy asks where to save a bare name instead of writing it to the working directory
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1212.

Share › Export as Web Page (and Save as Web Page in the native File menu) opens the small Save a Copy dialog, which asks for a name. A name typed there went straight to `file.exportHtml` as a relative path, so the page was written to the process's working directory: the install folder on Windows, `/` when launched from the Finder, wherever the launcher started it on Linux, never Documents or Downloads. Now a name without a folder goes to the save picker as its suggestion, so the user chooses where it lands; a full path is still written as typed, and an empty field opens the picker as before. Thanks to #394 and #641, which set up the HTML export and its error path; the export itself was fine.

#1213 looks like the same thing: its popup names a bare `testcsvexport.csv`, and Export as CSV goes through the same dialog, so on Windows the write hit the install folder and got "access denied". I haven't confirmed it on Windows, so I left that issue open.

Another option would be to drop the text field and have these menu entries open the picker directly, as File › Export already does; happy to switch if you prefer that.

body:
Number formats typed in Excel's Format Axis and Format Data Labels panes were lost: on import every axis and data label followed its source cells, and saving dropped them. In a set of 11 Excel-saved fleet reports, 10 such formats (6 axis, 4 data label) appear across 5 files: a duration axis (`[h]:mm`) next to a percentage axis (`0%`) on a combo chart, `#,##0` value axes, and `0;;;` labels (positives only, so zero bars carry no label). GridCraft saved none of them, and drew the Idling Violations axes as `0`…`1.0`.

## What changed

- **Model** (`crates/model/src/features.rs`). `Chart.axis_number_formats: AxisNumberFormats { x, y, y2 }` (the X value axis of scatter and bubble charts, the value axis, the secondary value axis) and `Series.label_number_format`. title: XLSX: keep the sensitivity label, table column data formats and sheet custom properties on save
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1209.

The table writer built `<table>` with only its id, name, range and row counts, and the reader never looked at the table-level format attributes, so a plain open and save dropped them. They're now read into a `TableFormats` on `Table`, following what #867 does for a column's `dataDxfId` / `dataCellStyle`: the six dxf ids (`headerRowDxfId`, `dataDxfId`, `totalsRowDxfId`, `headerRowBorderDxfId`, `tableBorderDxfId`, `totalsRowBorderDxfId`) are kept as styles and written back through the workbook's dxf list, and the three cell styles (`headerRowCellStyle`, `dataCellStyle`, `totalsRowCellStyle`) are written when that named style is still in the workbook, same rule as the column one.

title: Sheet tabs: right-clicking a tab activates its sheet
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
Right-clicking a sheet tab opens the tab menu but leaves the previously active sheet active. Excel activates the tab you right-click. This matters because some menu items act on the active sheet, not the clicked one:

- **Protect Sheet… / Unprotect Sheet…** reads and changes the active sheet. Right-click a protected tab while an unprotected sheet is active and the menu offers "Protect Sheet…", which then protects the other sheet.
- **Select All Sheets** and anything else in the menu that uses the active sheet has the same mismatch.

Insert Sheet, Delete, Rename, Move or Copy, Duplicate, Tab Color and Hide already take the clicked tab's index, so they were fine.

## Repro (0.6.1 and main 84acf62)
1. Make a workbook with sheets Data and Reference, and protect Reference.
2. With Data active, right-click the Reference tab.
3. The menu says "Protect Sheet…" and Data stays active. Excel switches to Reference and offers "Unprotect Sheet…".

## Change
`crates/ui-egui/src/tabs.rs`, `sheet_tabs`: a secondary click on an inactive tab activates its sheet (through the existing `activate_sheet`, so an open edit is committed first and point mode keeps working), before the menu reads the active sheet.

## Tests
- `right_clicking_a_tab_activates_its_sheet_so_the_menu_acts_on_it` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/sheet_tabs.rs`: right-clicks an inactive protected tab and checks it becomes active and the menu offers "Unprotect Sheet…". It fails on main and passes here.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers and wasm pass. `parity` fails the same way on unmodified main on Windows (line endings in the regenerated checklist).

Found while testing #1222 (padlock on protected tabs).

title: XLSX: keep a dxf's protection, font size and face, and the font parts it turns off
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1209.

The shared dxf writer (`<dxfs>` in `styles.xml`) dropped a differential format's `<protection>`, leaving an empty `<dxf/>`, never wrote the font's `sz` and `name`, and only wrote the font parts that were turned on, so `<b val="0"/>`, `<i val="0"/>` and `<u val="none"/>` were lost. A header dxf that turns bold off lost it, and the table style made the header bold again.

A dxf's `Style` reads its default parts as unset, so "bold off" or "locked, not hidden" can't be told from "not stated". The reader now records those in a small `DxfStated` on `Style`, only where the stated value matches the default (empty for cell formats and for formats made in the app), and keeps a stated face and size in the font. The writer writes them back, along with `scheme`. Nothing that renders conditional formats or tables reads the new field.

Thanks @richard1912 for finding these while testing #1221 on a real workbook.

Validation:
- `fixtures::dxf_font_and_parts_stated_at_their_defaults_survive_save`: four dxfs (font parts turned off, size/face/scheme at their defaults, a default protection, a non-default one, a non-default size and face), checked against the `<dxfs>` written on save. Fails on main (`<dxfs count="2"><dxf></dxf><dxf><font><b/></font></dxf>`), passes here
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-xlsx --lib -- tests::fixtures tests::roundtrip`, `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --lib -- cf::`
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-model -p gridcraft-xlsx -p gridcraft-engine -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Journal: cap by serialized size and keep a recording's start through trims
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1228.

Thanks @ds-8362 for the measurements, they made this easy to pin down. `Session::execute` capped the journal only by entry count (10,000, trimmed to 5,000), so a few `file.open` entries with their base64 could hold tens of MB. This adds a byte cap: each entry's serialized size is measured once when it's pushed and kept alongside, and past 64 MB the oldest entries go until the journal is under half, the same way the count cap works. The newest entry always stays, even if it's bigger than the cap on its own. 64 MB is my guess at a sensible value, happy to switch to whatever you prefer.

While in there I found that trimming left `Session::recording` pointing at the old index, so a recording that spanned a trim saved a script with zero steps. The index now shifts with the trim (saturating at 0). Steps the trim dropped are still lost.

I left `journal_params` alone on purpose. `automate.recordActions` turns journal entries into saved scripts, and `engine.journal` is documented as replayable, so swapping the base64 for a summary (name, size, hash) would stop a recorded `file.open` or `insert.picture` from replaying. If you'd rather have the summary and accept that trade-off, I can do it in a follow-up. Summarising large `range.setValues` arrays and paginating `engine.journal` are also still open.

Validation:
- `tests::journal_is_capped_by_serialized_size`: fails on main (12 entries of 8 MB stay in the journal, over the cap), passes here
- `tests::recording_keeps_its_steps_when_the_journal_is_trimmed`: fails on main (`{"recording":false,"saved":"Steps","steps":0}`), passes here
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --lib` on the journal tests, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: BAHTTEXT: a final one after the millions reads เอ็ด
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1234.

Thanks @EarthSR for the clear report. BAHTTEXT from #292 (thanks @vangel76) spells the number in groups of six digits, and `thai_group` decided between หนึ่ง and เอ็ด for a final 1 by looking only at the higher digits of its own group. After ล้าน the units group of 21,000,001 is `000001`, with no higher digit inside the group, so it came out as หนึ่ง. `thai_group` now also gets whether the number already has a non-zero digit in a higher group, so 1,000,001 reads หนึ่งล้านเอ็ด and 21,000,001 reads ยี่สิบเอ็ดล้านเอ็ด, as in Excel. A lone 1 stays หนึ่ง, and satang are unchanged (0.01 is หนึ่งสตางค์, 0.21 is ยี่สิบเอ็ดสตางค์).

The same rule now applies to the units before a second ล้าน (1,000,001,000,000 reads หนึ่งล้านเอ็ดล้าน), which follows the Thai reading rule; I couldn't check that one against Excel, so happy to switch if it differs.

Validation:
- `text::tests::bahttext`: fails on main (21000001 gives ยี่สิบเอ็ดล้านหนึ่งบาทถ้วน), passes here; new cases also cover 1000001, 1001, 11, 1, 0.01, 0.21, and 1250.5 / 0.25 unchanged
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-functions --lib text::tests::bahttext`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-functions --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Fonts: discover macOS assets and use PingFang SC for Chinese UI fallback
author: zxcbbn
body:
macOS stores stock PingFang outside the conventional font directories, and its 78,222,888-byte collection exceeds the scanner's 64 MiB limit. The installed-font catalog therefore omits PingFang even where it is available. The Chinese UI fallback also only checks the older fixed paths, so it cannot use this installed collection in filenames, Recent lists and other interface text.

This includes the versioned MobileAsset font directories under both macOS asset roots and raises the bounded file limit to 128 MiB. The Chinese fallback prefers the installed PingFang SC Regular face, identifies its collection index from font metadata, validates it before handing it to egui, and shares cached bytes across font/theme rebuilds. It reads only the named PingFang collection at startup, without waiting for the entire background font catalog. Existing fallback candidates remain available when PingFang is absent or unreadable, and the Japanese-first Han ordering is preserved. No font assets or new dependencies are bundled.

Validation on macOS arm64:
- Installed-font catalog and UI face-selection regressions each fail without their respective fixes.
- Synthetic catalog tests cover both asset roots, duplicate/missing directories, unrelated assets, a valid font padded to PingFang's size, and rejection above the new limit.

title: Web: the same file opened from bytes again switches to the open workbook
author: dev-exe
body:
Part of #1226.

## Why

On the web build, File › Open and dropped files go through `file.open {name, base64}`. That path always added a new document; only path opens checked for one already open. So reopening a file kept every earlier copy in memory. In the measurements in #1226, each copy of a 4.2 MB formula workbook took about 480 MB, and the ninth open trapped at wasm32's 4 GiB, losing every open workbook.

## What changes

`file.open` from bytes (no path):

- **Same name, same bytes:** switches to the open workbook (`alreadyOpen`), as opening an already-open path does.
- **Same name, different bytes:** refused, with a message to close the open workbook first. Excel also opens only one workbook per name.
- **When it checks:** before parsing, so a duplicate is never loaded. It compares a hash of the bytes, kept on the document (`DocState.content_hash`).

Path opens are unchanged.

## Tests

- `reopening_the_same_bytes_switches_to_the_open_workbook`: fails on main (a second copy opens) and passes here.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes locally (macOS arm64, Rust 1.99).

## Not in this PR

- **From #1226:** containing out-of-memory, telling the host after a trap, and a list of open workbooks on the web.
- **The journal (#1228):** #1230 covers it. This PR doesn't touch the journal and merges cleanly with #1230.
- **Other memory issues:** undo memory on large sheets (#1227) and the base footprint (#1229).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Preview text and fill colors on hover
author: aurialLoop
body: Currently, users must apply a font or fill color to see how it looks in their selected cells. Hover previews let them compare colors before committing a formatting change. This change adds live previews when hovering over Home’s Font Color and Fill Color palettes. The selected cells preview the hovered color; leaving or dismissing the palette restores their formatting, and clicking applies the color as one undoable edit. The preview supports theme colors, tints, standard colors, Automatic, and No Fill. Previews affect rendering only, leaving the workbook and undo history unchanged. They work in frozen panes and Page Layout view and preserve table styling and conditional-formatting precedence. ### Tests added Tests cover hover, mouse-leave and Escape; applying a color and undoing it; selected versus unselected text rendering; Automatic and No Fill; and matching previewed styling to committed styling for ordinary cells and tables. ### Validation - `cargo xtask ci` passed all eight checks, including workspace tests and WASM compilation. - Built and launched the packaged macOS app on Apple Silicon with Rust 1.99.0. - The contributor manually tested the packaged macOS app and confirmed the feature works. ### Visual example Built-in Quarterly Sales Dashboard with B5:C8 selected. #### Fill color preview Hovering a gold Fill Color swatch previews the fill on the selected cells without clicking. #### Font color preview Hovering a red Font Color swatch previews the text color while preserving the existing table fill.

title: Fix web clipboard copy on plain HTTP
author: justinjohn0306
body:
Fixes #1240.

The web app now captures the rich/plain payload during eframe copy and cut events and writes it synchronously through ClipboardEvent.clipboardData. title: Opening an XLSX with a part over 512 MB says how to get the data in
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1242.

Thanks @dev-exe for suggesting the error should tell people how to get unblocked. Opening an XLSX where one part unpacks to more than the reader's 512 MB per-part cap (`MAX_PART` in `crates/xlsx/src/package.rs`) used to say:

> We can't open 'book.xlsx': the file is too large: xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml expands to 540278731 bytes

It now says:

> We can't open 'book.xlsx': its part xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml unpacks to 515 MB, over GridCraft's limit of 512 MB for one part (a guard against damaged or malicious files). To open it, split the data across several sheets, since the limit applies to each part, or save the sheet as CSV, which keeps only its values.

The limit itself is unchanged: raising it, or streaming very large sheets, is your call.

I only suggest what the code actually lets through:
- Splitting across sheets works because the cap is per part (the 1 GB package total still applies).
- CSV import has no per-part or size cap beyond the 2 GB `read_file` limit.
- .xlsb is left out, which corrects my earlier comment: the XLSB import stops at 1 million cells and 64 MiB of text (`crates/xlsx/src/xlsb.rs`), far less than a 515 MB sheet holds.
- When the oversized part is not a worksheet (for example `xl/sharedStrings.xml`, which every sheet shares), splitting sheets doesn't help, so the message only suggests CSV.

`gridcraft_xlsx::oversized_part` finds the part from the zip directory's declared sizes, and the engine uses it only when `read_xlsx` returns `TooLarge`. A part that lies about its size and is caught while inflating keeps the old message.

It fails on main with the message above and passes here. It also covers the shared-strings case, a size just over the limit (shown as "more than 512 MB", never "512 MB"), and a package broken for another reason, which keeps its own error.

title: Headers: mark hidden columns and rows, split cursor and double-click to unhide (#1247)
author: richard1912
body:
Fixes #1247.

## What changes

Hidden columns and rows are now visible in the headers, and can be unhidden from there, as in Excel:

- **Marker:** where one or more columns or rows are hidden, the header draws a double divider at that boundary (K‖M, 26 / 28). It also shows at the start of the strip when column A or row 1 is hidden. The colour is `header_text` at 60%, so it reads in both themes.
- **Split cursor:** hovering just past the boundary (right of K‖M, below 26 / 28) shows a split cursor: two bars with arrows. The edge just before the boundary still resizes the visible column or row, with the usual resize cursor. There is no split cursor in the OS cursor set, so it is painted on a tooltip layer in place of the pointer while hovering.
- **Double-click** on the split cursor unhides the column or row (`home.unhideColumns` / `home.unhideRows`). Previously a double-click there ran AutoFit, which leaves an empty hidden column hidden.
- **Drag** from that edge already unhid the line by giving it a width; that is unchanged.

All of it is in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`: `paint_headers`, the header hover and double-click handling, and three small helpers (`hidden_around`, `hidden_col_edge` / `hidden_row_edge`, `paint_split_cursor`).

## Tests

- `headers_mark_the_edges_next_to_hidden_lines`: which header edges get the marker (hidden A, L and row 27).
- `the_edge_just_past_a_hidden_line_unhides_it`: the hit-test picks the hidden line only just past the boundary, not on the visible line's own edge.
- Checked by hand on Windows 11 in a release build: marker, cursor, double-click unhide and drag unhide for columns and rows.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers and wasm pass. `parity` fails because `docs/parity-checklist.md` is already out of date on main; this PR doesn't touch the command catalog.

title: Dialogs move by their title bar instead of staying pinned to the centre
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1250.

Every dialog is drawn by the same `egui::Window` in `dialogs::show`, placed with `.anchor(CENTER_CENTER, (0, -40))`. In egui an anchored window is not movable, so Find and Replace couldn't be dragged off the cells it is searching, and neither could Go To, Format Cells, Sort or any other dialog, since they all go through that one window. The window now opens at the same spot with `.pivot(CENTER_CENTER).default_pos(...)`, so the title bar drags it like Excel's and it stays where it is dropped while it is open. Since the position is kept per dialog id, a dialog reopened later in the session comes back where it was last left, which is also what Excel does; happy to reset it on each open if you prefer it always centred.

Validation:
- `crates/ui-egui/tests/dialog_move.rs`: drags the Find and Replace title bar by (+120, +80) and checks the window is still offset by exactly that after ten more frames; a second test does the same for Go To, Format Cells and Sort. Both fail on main (the window doesn't move, offset `[0 0]`) and pass here; swapping `default_pos` for `fixed_pos` makes them fail again.
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --test dialog_move --test zoom_dialog --test popup_dismissal --test protect_password --test committed_text_fields`
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `docs/ui-parity.md` updated (Dialogs section, revision history)

title: fix(mcp): prevent replay and validate remote replies
author: euisuh
body:
A remote mutation can execute before its reply is lost. Retrying the same serialized request then executes it twice. The bounded reply reader also accepts EOF-terminated JSON and can leave a stale stream usable after malformed or mismatched responses.

Reconnect before a fresh call when the old connection is closed or contains stray bytes. Once transmission starts, never replay on write/read/parse failure: discard the socket and report uncertain completion. Require a complete newline-terminated bounded reply and exact request ID; preserve correlated application errors and existing pre-dispatch id-less refusals. The next explicit inspection reconnects. This does not cancel a server-side command or guarantee exactly-once execution.

The current main's authentication/server behavior is unchanged; unmerged auth PRs #783/#834 modify the same backend and may need integration after either lands. No dependencies or schema changes.

Validation:
- Unchanged-source regressions observed a replayed mutation and incorrectly accepted valid JSON without a newline.
- MCP package: 26 tests passed, including invalid JSON/UTF8/status/error/ID, exact small framing limits, refusal preservation and timeout recovery.
- Full cargo xtask ci: all eight stages passed; 1,606 workspace tests passed, one existing ignored; formatting, strict Clippy, assets, 16-crate layers, 11 WASM packages, parity and keytips passed.
- Explicit native all-target workspace check passed. Root and independent Claude source review approved.
- Kernel partial-send was not artificially simulated; any possible write failure follows the same single no-retry path. No live workbook mutation, GUI or Windows/Linux runtime run claimed. Private craftrules unavailable (404); public instructions followed.

Closes #1006. Closes #1045.

title: Bound Undo history growth after bulk edits
author: derechopiano
body:
Repeated bulk formula edits could keep about 1.45 GB of old workbook snapshots alive because Undo stopped only at 100 steps. This change estimates the cell-band storage retained by each history step and removes the oldest steps once the estimated total exceeds 128 MiB. The newest edit always remains undoable, and ordinary small edits can still use the full 100-step history.

The estimate accounts for copy-on-write bands, formulas, and cell values; it is a history budget, not a hard cap on process memory. Undo and Redo use the same trimming policy. No UI behavior or file format changes are involved.

Fixes #1227.

Validation (updated 14 October 2026 for commit `72db972de306a165af5296cb2e5f932a19c0cc02`):
- `cargo xtask ci` passed locally on Windows: formatting, workspace Clippy, all workspace tests, assets, layering, WASM, parity, and keytips.
- GitHub CI passed independently.

This PR was opened before the required full local suite had finished because the drive was short of space. That was premature. After resolving the storage blocker without removing the existing GridCraft build cache, I reran the complete local gate on the unchanged PR commit. The local test environment also needed a writable temporary directory and permission for a loopback-socket integration test; the final run completed successfully.

title: N() converts a computed array element by element, so it works inside SUMPRODUCT
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1279.

N() is registered with an array parameter, so the automatic lifting never applies to it and `N(F1>B1:B2)` collapsed to its first element. SUMPRODUCT then got a single value next to two 2x1 arrays and returned #VALUE!. `--`, ABS(), VALUE() and the other scalar functions are lifted, which is why they work. I kept N() unlifted for references, since `N(A1:A3)` reads only the first cell, and made it convert a computed array (a comparison, an array constant) element by element. That changes the existing unit assertion `N({3,4}) = 3`: it now gives `{3,4}`, and the first-cell case is asserted on a range instead. Thanks @JamesCorliss for the minimal repro.

Validation:
- `calc::tests::n_lifts_over_a_computed_array_but_reads_the_first_cell_of_a_range` (the formula from the issue, `SUMPRODUCT(N(B1:B2>0))`, and `SUM(N(D2:D3))` reading only D2): fails on main (H1 = #VALUE!), passes here
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-functions --lib info::`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-functions -p gridcraft-calc --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: Sort: a Sheet! prefix on the range sorts that sheet, not the active one
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1283.

`do_sort` always wrote to `wb.active_sheet`, and `data_range` dropped the `Sheet!` prefix of `range`, so `data.sort` (and `sort_range`, which goes through it) sorted the same cells on the active sheet and reported success. Sort now resolves its sheet with the existing `target_sheet` helper, the way `range.setValues` and the formatting commands do, and passes it down to `do_sort`; `data.sortAscending`/`data.sortDescending` share that path, so they get the same fix. Following the rule in #885, the selection belongs to the active sheet, so naming another sheet without a `range` is an error, and so is a prefix that disagrees with `sheet`. Happy to switch to refusing a prefix that names another sheet instead (the #206 rule for cell references), if you'd rather keep sort on the active sheet.

Thanks @Essermarth for the precise repro. Other `data.rs` commands still read `active_sheet` directly (filter, remove duplicates, subtotal, circle invalid data); I left them out to keep this one small, happy to send them as a follow-up.

Validation:
- `tests::sort_with_a_sheet_prefix_sorts_the_named_sheet` (the steps from the issue): fails on main (`Prices` stays `p1, p2, p3`, Sheet1 gets sorted), passes here
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --lib sort`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: Remove Duplicates, Filter and Subtotal: a Sheet! prefix on the range works on that sheet, not the active one
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Follow-up to #1284, as @Essermarth asked there. Refs #1283.

`data.removeDuplicates`, `data.filter` and `data.subtotal` took a `range` such as `"Prices!A1:B4"`, dropped the sheet name, ran on the same cells of the active sheet and reported success. Now they work on the named sheet. They follow the same rules as #1284: if `sheet` and the prefix name different sheets it's an error, and naming another sheet without a `range` is an error too, because the selection belongs to the active sheet (#885). The check lives in a shared `data_target` helper in `cmd/data.rs`, which is #1284's `sort_target` made general. That overlaps #1284, so I'll rebase whichever of the two lands second and point the sort commands at the shared helper.

Covered:
- `data.removeDuplicates`
- `data.filter`: on another sheet, if a table there contains the first cell of `range`, the command toggles that table's filter button; otherwise it toggles the sheet AutoFilter on `range`. On the active sheet nothing changes: the active cell still decides, as today. That was my reading of the table case, happy to switch if you'd rather have it work another way.
- `data.subtotal`: `home.insertRows`, `cell.set` and `home.bold` already take `sheet`, so subtotal now passes it to them. `data.group` and `data.ungroup` gain an optional `sheet` parameter, resolved like the other commands. Naming another sheet without `rows` or `cols` is an error, for the same selection reason.

Notes, not part of this PR:
- `data.filterBy`, `data.clearFilter`, `data.reapply` and `data.circleInvalid` take no `range`, so there is no prefix to ignore. They work on the active sheet's AutoFilter or validations.
- `data.validate` refuses a `cell` that names another sheet instead of checking it there.

title: Linux: default to XWayland so the desktop draws the window frame
author: sudo-py-dev
body:
## Problem

On a GNOME Wayland session GridCraft's window has a black border and bare, square minimize/maximize/close buttons, while WordCraft on the same desktop gets the normal GNOME title bar.

GNOME's compositor (Mutter) draws no server-side frame for native Wayland windows, so winit falls back to its own minimal client-side frame. WordCraft avoids this because it runs through XWayland by default (storytold/wordcraft#220, originally for file drag-and-drop, which winit supports only on X11).

## Change

The same approach and code as WordCraft:

- `apps/gridcraft/src/main.rs`: on `cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "macos")))`, when `DISPLAY` is set and `GRIDCRAFT_WAYLAND` is not, the event loop is built with `with_x11()`, so the window runs through XWayland and the desktop draws its frame. `GRIDCRAFT_WAYLAND=1` keeps the native Wayland backend (the counterpart of `WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND`).
- `apps/gridcraft/Cargo.toml`: `winit = { version = "0.30", default-features = false, features = ["x11"] }` under the same target as WordCraft. It is already in the tree through eframe, so the only lockfile change is the new edge.
- `README.md`: a **Wayland** note in the Linux section about the default and the opt-out, like WordCraft's.

Side benefit: dragging files from the file manager into the window now works on Wayland desktops, as in WordCraft.

## Reviewer notes

- Flatpak is unchanged. Its manifests use `--socket=wayland` + `--socket=fallback-x11`, as WordCraft's do, so inside a Wayland session the sandbox has no `DISPLAY` and stays on native Wayland, exactly as WordCraft behaves.

- The trade-off, as for WordCraft, is XWayland's scaling with fractional display scaling; users who prefer native Wayland set `GRIDCRAFT_WAYLAND=1`.

title: Linux: default to XWayland so the desktop draws the window frame
author: sudo-py-dev
body:
## Summary

On Linux Wayland desktops, GNOME in particular, GridCraft's window had a **black border around the window and bare, square minimize/maximize/close buttons** in a dark strip above the app. WordCraft on the same desktop gets the normal GNOME title bar with rounded buttons and the document title. This PR makes GridCraft start the same way WordCraft does, so the desktop draws the window frame.

## Root cause

- GridCraft uses eframe/winit, which picks the **native Wayland backend** whenever `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set.
- On Wayland, window decorations are either drawn by the compositor (server-side, via `xdg-decoration`) or by the app itself (client-side).
- **GNOME's compositor (Mutter) does not implement server-side decorations** for Wayland clients. winit then draws its own minimal fallback frame (sctk-adwaita), which is what produced the black border and plain control boxes.
- WordCraft doesn't show this because it already defaults to **XWayland** (storytold/wordcraft#220, added there so file drag-and-drop works, since winit supports dropping files into a window only on X11). Under XWayland the window manager draws a full native frame, as for any X11 app.

## What changed

The same approach and code as WordCraft's #220, adapted only for the names:

### `apps/gridcraft/src/main.rs`
- On `cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "macos")))` (Linux and the BSDs, as in WordCraft), when `DISPLAY` is set (XWayland is available) and `GRIDCRAFT_WAYLAND` is **not** set, the eframe event loop is built with `EventLoopBuilderExtX11::with_x11()`.
- `GRIDCRAFT_WAYLAND=1` keeps the native Wayland backend, the counterpart of WordCraft's `WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND=1`.
- Pure X11 sessions are unaffected (they already used X11), and so are Wayland sessions without XWayland (`DISPLAY` unset, so winit picks Wayland as before).

title: Linux: build an Arch package (.pkg.tar.zst)
author: ujo4eva
body:
Adds an Arch Linux package to the Linux release, next to the `.deb` and `.rpm`. Arch users (Manjaro, EndeavourOS, Omarchy, ...) can then `sudo pacman -U` it, and ArtCraft Launcher can install and update it through pacman (storytold/craft-launcher#389).

## What changes

- `packaging/linux/package.sh`:
  - adds an `arch` format, on by default;
  - builds `gridcraft-<ver>-linux-<arch>.pkg.tar.zst` with nfpm's `archlinux` packager from the same `nfpm.yaml`.

  nfpm can't rename a package per format and doesn't env-expand `archlinux.packager`, so the script writes a copy of the config with both set.
- `packaging/linux/nfpm.yaml`:
  - an `overrides.archlinux` block with Arch dependencies: `glibc gcc-libs hicolor-icon-theme libxkbcommon vulkan-icd-loader`;
  - `provides: gridcraft`;
  - `conflicts: gridcraft, gridcraft-bin, gridcraft-git`.
- **Named `ai.storyteller.gridcraft`, not `gridcraft`.** The AUR already has `gridcraft`, `gridcraft-bin` and `gridcraft-git`. An AUR helper treats an installed package with an AUR name as its own and would rebuild it on the next update. The bundle id is also how the launcher tells this package (which it updates) from an AUR build (which it leaves to the AUR helper).
- The README's Linux download table gains an Arch row.

**No workflow change is needed.** `craft-common-actions` uploads and checksums everything `package.sh` writes to `dist/release`, and the riscv64 job passes `--formats "deb rpm tar"`.

## Notes

- nfpm has no `optdepends` for Arch, so the Debian `recommends` have no Arch equivalent.
- Pre-releases sort correctly: `0.7.0-rc.1` becomes pkgver `0.7.0rc.1`, which pacman places before `0.7.0`. Arm64 maps to `aarch64`.

## Testing

- I ran `package.sh --skip-build --formats arch` with the binaries from the published v0.6.1 x86_64 tarball, checked against `SHA256SUMS.txt`. It produced `gridcraft-0.6.1-linux-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst`.

title: Keyboard: Ctrl+Q no longer closes GridCraft and drops unsaved work
author: iluebbe
body:
On Windows and Linux, Ctrl+Q closed GridCraft at once, without asking to save, so unsaved work was lost. The same went for Ctrl+Shift+Q and Ctrl+Alt+Q.

## Problem

egui closes the window on `Options::quit_shortcuts`, which defaults to Ctrl/Cmd+Q (`egui 0.36.2`, `Context` sends `ViewportCommand::Close`). It matches the shortcut logically, so extra Shift or Alt still count. GridCraft cancels a close request only while printing (`apps/gridcraft/src/main.rs`), and the window closes without the Save Changes prompt.

- **Excel:** on Windows, Ctrl+Q is Quick Analysis (#791, #795). It never quits.
- **German keyboard:** AltGr+Q types `@`, and Windows reports AltGr as Ctrl+Alt. If egui receives that key as Ctrl+Alt+Q, typing `@` closes the window. I checked this in the test harness, not with a German keyboard in the running app.
- **macOS:** Cmd+Q is the app's Quit, as the menu bar shows. It stays.

## Fix

`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`: outside macOS, `quit_shortcuts` is cleared once, next to the existing `zoom_with_keyboard` override. The window still closes through its close button and through `app.quit`. #795 (Quick Analysis) binds Ctrl+Q to its own command; that PR doesn't change the quit shortcut, so the two don't overlap.

## Testing

- `ctrl_q_does_not_close_the_window` (`crates/ui-egui/tests/keyboard_shortcuts.rs`, kittest): on Windows and Linux, Ctrl+Q, Ctrl+Shift+Q and Ctrl+Alt+Q send no `ViewportCommand::Close` while a workbook has unsaved input. Without the fix, the test fails on the first press ("Windows … closed the window").
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers and wasm pass.
  - `parity` and `keytips` report their generated files out of date on this Windows checkout (`core.autocrlf`).
  - Regenerating them changes only line endings: `git diff` is empty, as on `main`.

title: Filter: count empty text and ="" results as (Blanks) (#1294)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1294.

The AutoFilter's (Blanks) group only matched `Value::Empty`. A formula such as `=""` evaluates to `Value::Text("")`, and imported empty shared strings look the same, so these cells were hidden when only (Blanks) was ticked and showed up as their own empty entry in the dropdown.

Changes in `crates/engine/src/cmd/data.rs`:
- New `filter_blank` predicate: an empty cell or zero-length text. It is filter-specific; `Value::is_empty`, Go To Special `blanks` and formula storage are unchanged.
- `apply_filter` uses it for the (Blanks) check of a values criterion.
- `filter_values` (the dropdown list) uses it too, so these cells fold into the single (Blanks) entry, sorted last like before.

Whitespace (`" "`) and zero are still not blanks. Slicers already skip empty display text when listing tiles, so they are consistent with this.

Test: `filter_blanks_include_empty_text_and_formula_results` runs the issue's repro (empty, `=""`, space, zero; filter by (Blanks) only). It checks that only the space and zero rows are hidden, and that the dropdown has one (Blanks) entry and no empty-text entry. Both checks fail without the fix.

title: Conditional formatting: data bars keep Automatic vs Lowest/Highest bounds and their lengths
author: iluebbe
body:
Fixes #1158 and #1159. Data bars told Excel's Automatic bounds and Lowest/Highest Value apart nowhere, and drew every bar from 0 with a fixed 10 % head start.

**Builds on #717** (Excel 2010 conditional formats, @neilcawse). That PR moves the x14 data bar reader and writer this one extends, so this branch starts from its head (6f0f747) and contains its four commits until it merges. Please merge #717 first; I'll rebase this one onto `main` then.

## Problem

- **Bounds (#1159).** Excel writes both Automatic and Lowest/Highest Value as `<cfvo type="min"/>` / `max` in the main section; only the x14 rule tells them apart (`autoMin`/`autoMax`). GridCraft read both as `Min`/`Max` and evaluated `Min` as Automatic. It wrote its own bars without x14 bounds, which Excel reads as Lowest/Highest Value. So a bar made in GridCraft looked different in Excel, and an Excel bar with Lowest Value looked different in GridCraft.
- **Lengths (#1158).** `CfCache::look` pulled every positive minimum to 0 and drew `frac × 0.9 + 0.1`. A bar with a fixed minimum (Number, Percent, Percentile, Formula, Lowest Value) was too long, and a value at the minimum got half a bar instead of none. The bar lengths in the file (`minLength`/`maxLength`) were ignored.

## Fix

- **Model** (`features.rs`):
  - `CfValueKind::AutoMin` and `AutoMax`, documented as data-bar only.
  - `CfRule::DataBar` gets `min_length` and `max_length` (percent of the cell). The serde defaults are 10 and 90, a file's defaults.
- **Evaluation** (`cf.rs`):
  - Automatic minimum: 0, or the lowest value when that is negative, as before. Every other minimum is used as it is.
  - The bar is `minLength + frac × (maxLength − minLength)` of the cell, with `frac = (value − min) / (max − min)` clamped to 0…1.
- **XLSX read** (`sheet_read.rs`):
  - `autoMin`/`autoMax` become `AutoMin`/`AutoMax`.
  - The x14 rule a main-section bar links to now gives its bounds and lengths as well as its fill. The main section's `minLength`/`maxLength` are re…

title: Conditional formatting: rules follow copied, cut and filled cells; Clear Formats removes them
author: iluebbe
body:
Fixes #1164. In GridCraft, conditional formats stayed where they were when cells were copied, cut, filled or had their formats cleared, and Clear Rules from Selected Cells deleted every rule the selection touched.

## Problem

In Excel a conditional format is part of the cells' formatting: it travels with copied, cut and filled cells, and Clear Formats removes it. GridCraft moved a rule's range only for inserted and deleted rows, columns and cells:
- copy, cut, fill, AutoFill and Format Painter left rules where they were;
- Clear Formats and Clear All didn't remove them;
- `clear_cf` dropped every range that intersected the selection, so clearing the rules of A5 removed the rule from all of A1:A10.

## Measured in Excel for Microsoft 365

Excel was driven through COM in its own instance, with no clipboard: `Range.Copy`/`Cut` with a destination, `FillDown`, `AutoFill`, `FormatConditions.Delete`, `ClearFormats`, `Clear`. Each case starts from a rule "greater than 5" on the range shown and lists the rules' ranges afterwards, by priority. All 46 cases are in `rules_follow_their_cells_as_in_excel`. They show these rules:

| Action | Excel | For example |
|---|---|---|
| Clear Rules from Selected Cells, Clear Formats, Clear All | The selected cells leave the rule. What is left of a rectangle is listed above, below, left, right. | A1:C10, clear B5 → `A1:C4,A6:C10,A5,C5` |
| Clear Contents | No change | |
| Fill Down, AutoFill | The source cells' rule widens | A1:A10, AutoFill to A1:C10 → `A1:C10` |
| Copy, rule stays one line of cells | Joins the rule it came from | A2 → A11: `A1:A11`; A1:J1 → K1: `A1:T1`; A1:A10 → A5: `A1:A14` |
| Copy, anything else | A new rule, on top | A1:A10 → B1: `B1:B10 \| A1:A10`; A1:C10 → A11: `A11:C20 \| A1:C10` |
| Copy next to an earlier copy | Another new rule (only the source rule is joined) | A1:A10 → C1, then → C11: `C11:C20 \| C1:C10 \| A1:A10` |
| Cells without a rule pasted over rule cells | They leave the rule | E1 → A5: `A1:A4,A6:A10`…

title: Table references: Excel parity for fill, rename, point mode and colours; Table[rows][columns] lookups
author: anton-belkin
body:
Table references: Excel's behaviour for filling, renaming, pointing and colouring, plus name-based lookups (`Table[rows][columns]`) that are saved as plain Excel formulas.

Full description: [`docs/table-reference-extensions.md`](docs/table-reference-extensions.md).

## Excel feature parity

Observed in Excel for Mac 16.113.4 with synthetic workbooks (clean-room: behaviour only, nothing committed from Excel).

| Behaviour | Excel | GridCraft before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Fill sideways** (fill handle, Fill Right) moves the columns of structured references along the table: `Table1[Price]` → `Table1[Stock]` → … | yes; past the last column it wraps to the first | columns never moved | same as Excel |
| **Copy / paste** keeps structured references unchanged | yes | yes | yes |

title: Options: User name; a save records who saved the workbook and when
author: iluebbe
body:
File › Options gets a **User name**, and a save now records who saved the workbook and when, as Excel does. Before, the name could only be changed by editing `prefs.json`, and an Excel file saved in GridCraft lost its *Last Modified By* and its dates.

## Problem

- `Prefs::user_name` exists and signs new notes and comments, but it starts as `GridCraft User` and nothing in the app or the command set changes it (only the web host's `?author=`).
- A new workbook never gets an author, and a save never records who saved it.
- `docProps/core.xml` is read and written with title, subject, creator, keywords and description only. `cp:lastModifiedBy`, `dcterms:created` and `dcterms:modified` are dropped when a file is opened, so they are gone after the next save.

Excel's reference behaviour (public documentation, not observed for this PR): File › Options › General › *Personalize your copy* holds the user name; it becomes the author of new workbooks and the *Last Modified By* of every save; File › Info lists *Related Dates* (Created, Last Modified) and *Related People* (Author, Last Modified By).

## Change

- **`options.userName`** `{name?}` (engine, `cmd/file.rs`): sets the user name or, without `name`, reports it. Control characters become spaces, the ends are trimmed, at most 200 characters are kept (the web host's `?author=` cap), and a blank name is refused.
- **File › Options › General › User name**: a text field that commits when it loses focus (Enter or a click elsewhere), with a one-line note on what the name is used for. An emptied field keeps the saved name: an error raised by Enter would be closed by the same key press, so it is not sent.
- **Desktop start**: while no name was chosen, the app uses the account's name (`USERNAME`, else `USER` / `LOGNAME`). A `prefs.json` that holds the old placeholder counts as unchosen, since every existing install saved it without anyone choosing it. Runs with `GRIDCRAFT_NO_PREFS` are unchanged.
- **Save** (`file.save`, Save As, …

title: AutoFit Column Width measures text in the font the grid draws it with
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1316.

`home.autofitColumnWidth` sized columns from `approx_text_width`, a table of average glyph widths, and the comment promising that the UI would refine it with real measurement had nothing behind it. When the cell's font is substituted with a wider one (Noto Sans for Calibri on Linux, as in the report), or the text has wide glyphs like `@` and `%`, the column came out too narrow and the end of the text was clipped. Thanks @KnottyDyes for the measurements and for pointing straight at the cause.

The engine still has no fonts, so `Session` gets an optional `text_width` measure. The egui app installs one that lays the line out in the face `theme::cell_family` picks for the cell, the same one the grid draws with, and AutoFit uses it with the existing padding. Each distinct text is measured once per AutoFit, and past 2,000 distinct values the measure sums glyph advances instead of laying the text out, so a huge column doesn't build a galley per row; the sum has no kerning (plus half a point for the galley's rounding), so it errs on the wide side. The CLI and MCP have no measure and keep the estimate. If a family isn't in the active font set yet (bound fonts apply from the next frame), the measure falls back to the estimate instead of letting egui panic. I left the other `approx_text_width` callers (PivotTable column fit, wrapped row height) and #1261 alone; happy to extend the measure to those too, or to shape it differently (e.g. a param on the command), if you prefer.

Validation:
- `header_double_click_fits_the_text_as_the_grid_draws_it` (crates/ui-egui/tests/header_autofit.rs): double-clicks the header divider and checks the column holds the text as the grid draws it plus padding. Fails on main (`column 233 is narrower than the drawn text 267.4 + padding`), passes here; also fails again if AutoFit ignores the measure
- `autofit_measures_each_distinct_text_once_and_quickly_past_the_limit` (engine) and `the_quick_measure_is_never_narrower_than_the_drawn_tex…

title: Shapes: select, resize from every handle and rotate
author: fluorine
body: ## What Clicking an inserted shape (rectangle, ellipse, arrow…) looked like it did nothing: the shape was selected (`selected_chart` was set, drag-to-move and the bottom-right corner already worked), but only text boxes drew a selection frame, so there was no feedback and no way to see the handles. This PR fixes that and brings shape handling up to what a user expects from Excel: - **Selection frame on every selected object** — eight handles (corners only when the frame is under 40 px on an axis). Charts, pictures and slicers use the same frame. - **Resize from any handle** — the opposite side stays put; Shift keeps the aspect ratio on a corner. Before, only the bottom-right corner resized. - **Rotation** — a rotation handle above the top edge turns the shape; Shift snaps to 15°. A turned shape paints (fill, outline, text), hit-tests and resizes along its own axes. One drag is one undo step. - **Cursors** — each handle shows the resize cursor for its on-screen direction (follows the rotation); the body shows Move; the rotation handle shows a crosshair. - **Keys on a selected object** — arrows nudge it 6 pt (Ctrl/Alt: 1 pt) instead of moving the cell cursor, Escape deselects it, Enter/F2 edits a text box. Logic was based on functionality of Shapes in **WordCraft**. ## Model, file format and commands - `Shape.rotation`: degrees clockwise about the centre, `#[serde(default)]` so older workbooks load. - XLSX reads and writes it as the shape's `a:xfrm rot` (60000ths of a degree). - `object.move` takes `rotation` for shapes and refuses it for charts, pictures and slicers (they have no angle in the model). No new command id; the UI drag, the control channel, CLI and MCP all go through `object.move`. The handle geometry lives in a new `crates/ui-egui/src/frame.rs` (handles, grab test, turned resize, angle-to-pointer), kept UI-only per the layering. ## Screenshots

title: packaging: RPM requires library sonames, so openSUSE can install it
author: tydude001
body:
## What and why

GridCraft's RPM requires Fedora package names: `libxkbcommon`, `(vulkan-loader or libglvnd-egl)`.
openSUSE has no `libxkbcommon`, `vulkan-loader` or `libglvnd-egl` package, so zypper refuses it with
`nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` (exit 4, which the ArtCraft Launcher shows as "error 4";
storytold/craft-launcher#341).

This requires the libraries' sonames instead, as PhotoCraft and VectorCraft already do, so the same RPM
resolves on Fedora/RHEL and openSUSE. It also declares the binaries' glibc floor, matching the deb's
`libc6 (>= 2.35)`. The floor names libm, not libc: the
binaries' only GLIBC_2.35 symbols are `hypot` and `hypotf` from libm, and RHEL 9's current glibc
(`2.34-283.el9_8`) provides `libc.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)` through backports but not libm's.

## How it was tested

GridCraft 0.6.1's released x86_64 binaries, repackaged with nfpm 2.47.0 and this branch's `nfpm.yaml`, then
installed with the distro's own package manager in a fresh x86_64 container and run with `gridcraft-cli --version`.
The released RPM is the same test on the release's own package.

| | released 0.6.1 RPM | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Fedora 44 | installs, runs | installs, runs |
| openSUSE Tumbleweed | `nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` | installs, runs |
| openSUSE Leap 15.6 | `nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` | installs, runs |
| Rocky Linux 9 (glibc 2.34) | installs; `gridcraft-cli`: ``libm.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.35' not found`` | refused: `nothing provides libm.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)(64bit)` |

The aarch64 RPMs get the same requires. I checked that side on FilmCraft only: its 0.7.2 arm64 binaries need
GLIBC_2.35 for the same two libm symbols, and its branch RPM installs and runs on arm64 Fedora 44,
Tumbleweed and Leap 15.6 (qemu-user).

`cargo xtask ci` passes. This tests installation and the CLI, not the GUI. The same results for every
Crafting App: https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/issues/341#issuecomment-6171570045

title: MCP: acknowledge successful commands without results
author: derechopiano
body:
When `execute_command` runs a successful command that returns `null` (for example `home.columnWidth`, `home.rowHeight`, or `pageLayout.orientation`), MCP now returns `{"ok": true}`. Commands that return data retain that data, and errors remain errors. The acknowledgement means the call succeeded; it does not claim the workbook changed.

Adds a regression test for the three reported layout commands, a data-returning command, and a missing-parameter error. Updates the MCP tool description and docs.

Fixes #1291.

Validation: `cargo xtask ci` passed locally on the v0.7.0 `main` base before commit, in the pre-commit hook, and in the pre-push hook.

title: Reject a list data validation that has no formula1 (#1303)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Part of #1303 (the missing `formula1` case).

`data.validation` with `type: "list"` and no `formula1` (for example `source` used by mistake) used to succeed and store a list rule with an empty source, so every value was rejected afterwards. It now returns a bad-params error ("a list validation needs `formula1`"), so `gridcraft-cli run --cmd` exits non-zero, like the other required-parameter errors in `data.rs` (`data.filterBy` "missing `column`"). An empty or `=`-only `formula1` is treated as missing. Nothing is stored when the command fails.

Other validation types are unchanged, and the Data Validation dialog always sends `formula1` for a list rule.

Not changed here: the issue also asks for unknown parameter names (such as `"bogus":1` on `cell.set`) to be rejected for every command. That is a change to command dispatch for all commands and needs a maintainer decision, so I left it out of this PR.

Test: `list_validation_without_formula1_is_an_error` covers the `source` typo from the issue, a missing `formula1`, and checks that a list rule with `formula1` still accepts a listed value.

title: Slicer: find a named table on any sheet
author: dev-exe
body:
## Problem

`insert.slicer` and `table.insertSlicer` only looked for the named table on the active sheet. When another sheet was open, adding a slicer to a table by name failed with "Select a cell inside a table first, or pass `table`", even though `table` was passed.

## Fix

- A table named in `table` is now found on any sheet, the same way other table commands find tables.
- The slicer goes on that table's sheet.
- `at` is checked against that sheet, so `"Sheet1!G2"` works.
- A name that matches no table now gives "no table named `X`".
- Without `table`, nothing changes.

## Tests

A new test, `slicer_finds_a_named_table_on_another_sheet`, makes a table on Sheet1, opens another sheet, and adds a slicer by the table's name. It checks the slicer lands on Sheet1 and filters the table. It fails on main and passes here.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine` all pass.

## Other open PRs

- #719 also changes `insert_slicer`, in a different part of the function. The two PRs merge cleanly, and all the slicer tests pass with both.
- #959 only changes the xlsx crate.

title: Formula parser: Excel's 8,192-character limit and postfix nesting (never crash)
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
## What this changes

A hostile file could abort any process that opens it, GridCraft included: a cell formula of about a million `%` (`=1%%%…`) or a 200,000-term sum (`=1+1+…`) parsed into trees deep enough to overflow the stack when printed, saved, evaluated or dropped — even in release builds. Postfix operators (`%`, invoking a result) built their nesting in a loop that the 256-level limit did not see.

- `parse` refuses formula text longer than Excel's 8,192 characters (`MAX_FORMULA_LEN`, counted in characters, the leading `=` excluded). This also bounds the depth of the left-deep trees long operator chains build.
- Each postfix `%` and each call of a result now counts towards the nesting limit.
- A formula from a file that is refused keeps its text and cached value, as other unparsable formulas do.

## Tests

- `formula`: `hostile_formulas_are_errors_not_stack_overflows` (small-stack thread: long `%`, invoke and operator chains are errors) and `formulas_longer_than_excel_allows_are_refused` (the limit counts characters, not bytes).
- `xlsx`: `hostile_formula_text_does_not_overflow_the_stack` — open, save and drop a workbook with such formulas and a defined name on a 1 MiB stack.
- Both regression tests abort with a stack overflow without the fix.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, and `cargo xtask` assets / layers / `parity --check` / `keytips --check` pass. `cargo xtask wasm` was not run (no wasm32 target installed on the machine used).

title: Form dialogs open ready to type (Column Width, Row Height)
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
In Excel, Alt+H, O, W opens Column Width with the value selected, so you type the new width and press Enter. In GridCraft the field didn't have focus, so you had to click into it first.

Form dialogs now open with the cursor in their first text or number field and its value selected:

- The first field takes focus once it can (a new window's first frame is a sizing pass that ignores focus requests), and its value is selected so typing replaces it.
- Number fields commit while typing. Before, Enter or OK in the same frame confirmed the old value, because a number field only committed when it lost focus.

Tests: `tests/dialog_focus.rs` (Column Width and Row Height: type a value, press Enter, the new value is applied). `cargo xtask ci` passes.

The oversized dialog box from the same flow is #978, which this PR doesn't touch.

title: Keyboard: Alt+= no longer starts an edit with the `=` it types
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1327.

On Windows and Linux, Alt+= arrives as the key press followed by the `=` the OS types with it. The grid's key handler ran AutoSum for the key, then took the `=` as typing and started an edit holding just `=` over the new total; committing that edit is the "unexpected `)`" message. The grid already ignores the text of Ctrl and Shift+Space shortcuts; this extends the same idea to any shortcut `keymap::dispatch` handled in that frame, so its character no longer starts an edit. AltGr combinations are unaffected (dispatch declines them, so their text still types), and on macOS Option+= still types `≠`, since Excel for Mac's AutoSum is Cmd+Shift+T.

Validation:
- `keyboard_shortcuts::alt_equals_autosum_does_not_also_type_the_equals_sign` sends the real key + text events for a column above, a row to the left, a block and an empty neighbourhood (`=SUM()`): fails on main (`Alt+= on A4 started an edit`), passes here
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --test keyboard_shortcuts`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Floating objects slide under frozen panes instead of covering them
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1328.

The cells are painted pane by pane with their own clip (`paint_panes`), but `chartview::paint_objects` painted every floating object (shapes, pictures, charts, slicers) with a single clip over the whole cell area, so an object in the scrolling pane was drawn on top of the frozen rows and columns once scrolled under them. This adds `Geo::object_area`, which clips each object to the pane its anchor sits in, as Excel does: objects in the scrolling pane slide under the frozen panes. An object anchored in the frozen rows/columns isn't cut at the freeze line, so it keeps the part that reaches into the scrolling pane (that part stays put instead of scrolling; happy to switch to drawing it per pane if you'd rather match Excel more closely there). `hit` and `slicer_click` use the same area, so a click on a frozen heading over a hidden picture selects the cell instead of the picture. The chart source-data highlight keeps its cell-space clip, the same `range_panes` approach as #217 for the selection.

Validation:
- `cell_pictures::floating_pictures_slide_under_the_frozen_top_row` (freezes row 1, scrolls a picture anchored at B5 half under it, checks the picture's clip, the hit test and a picture anchored in the frozen row): fails on main (the picture's clip starts at the top of the cell area, over the frozen row), passes here
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --test cell_pictures --test right_to_left --test freeze_handles --test chart_resize`
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- I left the docs alone (no `ui-parity.md` revision row) to avoid conflicts on the shared header line; happy to add one.

title: perf: accelerate large-workbook navigation and filtering
author: Miguel249
body:
## Problem and behavior

Large-sheet navigation repeatedly scanned stored cells for scrollbar bounds and rebuilt dimension indexes. Conditional-format painting also cloned complete range statistics per visible cell and computed those statistics for cell-local rules. Filtering formatted/cloned values unnecessarily and rebuilt an unchanged dependency graph.

This change adds bounded, invalidated bounds/geometry caches, borrows conditional-format statistics, prepares filter predicates once, and reuses dependencies for filter-only changes. All formulas are still evaluated; workbooks with tables conservatively retain the full rebuild.

## Measured results

Same Windows machine, release builds, original `d9d09f0` versus this implementation; two opposite-order pairs, five repetitions per operation and 100 CPU frames per run. The real XLSX contains 100,000 data rows and 300,012 formulas.

| Metric | Original | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Navigation CPU frame p95 | 518–524 ms | 6.21–6.25 ms |
| Filter p50, both selectivities/pairs | 1.86–2.40 s | 1.28–1.43 s |
| Complete open p50 | 4.91–5.40 s | 4.81–5.18 s |
| Peak working set | 2.83–2.84 GB | 2.81 GB |
| Formulas evaluated per filter | 300,012 | 300,012 |

CPU-frame p95 decreases approximately 98.8%; filtering decreases 23–47%. These CPU timings exclude tessellation/GPU/presentation and do **not** demonstrate actual FPS. Opening has no stable improvement; the real-file <4 s opening and <500 ms filter targets remain unmet. Peak memory changes are small.

Deterministic A–H benchmarks include mixed data/styles, sparse sheets, dependency chains, 500,000 rows and 1,000,000 rows. Native examples and a PowerShell wrapper record compiler/hardware, hashes, percentiles and peak working set. Production profiling is opt-in and adds no per-cell clocks. The user workbook and raw logs are not committed.

title: Selection: whole columns and rows don't widen to merged cells
author: DCM4711
body:
## Clicking a column header selects only that column, even across merged cells
